Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

According to recent reports, boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

Recent findings suggest that “We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” states Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:21.

Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.

The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.

PSG had maintained a perfect record across all competitions for nearly three months before Roma visited in the Champions League in midweek, with the Serie A side battling to a 2-2 draw on matchday five.

That result ended the Parisians' four-match European winning streak, although Luis Enrique's men remain second in the league-phase standings and firmly inside the coveted top-eight places that guarantee last-16 qualification.

Returning to league action should please supporters, who have watched their side claim eight consecutive victories since losing to Monaco at the start of September, albeit with only three clean sheets.

However, eagle-eyed observers will note that the Red and Blues have won only one of their last five meetings with Lorient across the past four years, with three of the last four encounters ending level.

Another draw would please Paris FC, Lille and Lyon, who trail the capital club by three, five and six points respectively as the Ligue 1 title race begins to take shape.

Alexandre Dujeux therefore aims to prevent Lorient's first defeat in this fixture since April 2024; however, his own five-match winless record against PSG and four consecutive losses to Enrique are ominous signs for the 50-year-old manager.

An indifferent run of results further undermines confidence in Les Merlus extending their unbeaten sequence in this fixture, with the Brittany-based club winning only one of their last four league matches.

Admittedly, only one of those matches ended in defeat, a 2-0 home loss to Brest, while their solitary victory during that period came away at Le Havre.

However, that early-November success offers limited encouragement given that it came against the division's bottom side, who have collected a paltry two points from 11 matches.

Their overall away record is more encouraging, with Dujeux's team conceding just twice across five matches on the road, both in September's 2-1 defeat to Le Mans, while keeping clean sheets in the other four.

Another shutout would make Lorient the first team since Monaco in November last year to prevent PSG from scoring, a feat far easier mentioned than done.

Paris Saint-Germain Ligue 1 form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue are both sidelined with ACL injuries for PSG's fixture on Saturday.

Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos are pushing for their first starts since last month's 4-2 victory over Barcelona, although Enrique may be tempted to retain the centre-back partnership of Ilya Zabarnyi and Willian Pacho.

Ferran Torres remains the capital club's leading Ligue 1 scorer with five goals, while Achraf Hakimi, Senny Mayulu and Marquinhos have three apiece.

Lorient have shared the goals around this season, with nine different players finding the net for the Brittany-based visitors.

Only Jean-Victor Makengo has scored more than once for Les Merlus, leaving Dujeux searching for someone to step up at Parc des Princes.

The visitors' prospects are further weakened by the absence of Panos Katseris, with a muscle injury ruling their leading goal provider out of this weekend's encounter.

Isaak Toure (groin) and Bandiougou Fadiga (muscle) are also sidelined for the 10th-placed side on matchday 12.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Pacho, Marquinhos, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Godts.

Lorient possible starting lineup:.

Mvogo; Adjei, Talbi, Obaretin; Sylla, Cadiou, Ebong, Kouassi; Makengo, Bernardeau; Tosin.

Lorient's four clean sheets from five away matches suggest that PSG may need patience, particularly against opponents who have repeatedly frustrated them in recent meetings.

However, the visitors' limited scoring threat and Katseris's absence should allow Enrique's men to sustain pressure and eventually secure a ninth consecutive league victory.

Leading the line for the visitors in West London, Dominic-Calvert-Lewin is also supposedly on the verge of putting pen to paper on fresh terms at Elland Road, with Leeds closing in on the striker's renewed signature.

Losing just two matches in the top flight so far this term, Leeds are currently occupying seventh position in the Premier League standings, with the Yorkshire giants targeting European qualification.

Aiming to record three straight league wins for the first time this campaign, Farke's side will be the heavy favourites on Saturday afternoon, when they welcome former Championship foes Coventry City to Elland Road.

According to Sky Sports News, Leeds are moving decisively ahead of a busy festive period on the pitch, with the European hopefuls aiming to resolve the long-term futures of Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka.

The report states that the Whites are closing in on a contract extension for Japanese midfielder Tanaka, whose current deal at Elland Road expires at the conclusion of the 2027-28 domestic cycle.

It is understood that Farke's side have offered the ex-Fortuna Dusseldorf man an extra 12 months of contract security, meaning that he is set to be committed to the cause until June 2029.

At the beginning of the calendar year, there was a real question mark over whether Tanaka had a future in the first-team ranks of Leeds, who were comfortably avoiding a relegation battle without the 28-year-old in their starting XI.

However, the engine-room enforcer has since fought his way back to the front of the plans for the Whites, with the midfielder starting nine of the club's 11 Premier League fixtures in 2026-27 so far.

Given the positive trajectory of Leeds over the past few years, it is no surprise that contract extensions are the talk of the town at the moment, with the club's hierarchy keen to tie their best assets down.

On the pitch, Tanaka and Calvert-Lewin have been key to the first-team progression at Elland Road, with the Whites looking set to establish themselves as a Premier League regular over the coming years.

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 10:16.

Former Manchester United star Gordon Strachan - speaking exclusively to Sports Mole - has urged the Red Devils to sign a £62.8m midfielder to help correct their "phenomenal" transfer mistakes.

New Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino remains winless since replacing Michael Carrick following Wednesday's infuriating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, in which the Red Devils fell behind, took the lead and were then pegged back in Portugal.

The four-goal stalemate marked the seventh game in a row that Man United had conceded at least two goals, and once again, the Red Devils' open midfield was exposed.

The pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo did not cover themselves in glory against Liverpool or Sporting, and the former is now suspended for RB Leipzig in December after being sent off towards the end of Wednesday's game.

Andrey Santos has also not yet had the desired impact since joining from Chelsea, while fellow 22-year-old Carlos Baleba has played just 397 minutes across seven appearances due to injury problems.

Speaking to Sports Mole via William Hill betting site, Strachan - who scored 36 goals in 198 games for Man United - has told the Red Devils hierarchy to make a move for Crystal Palace lynchpin Adam Wharton to help offset the "phenomenal" amount of money the club has wasted on under-performing players.

Sources indicate that "Adam Wharton is one of my picks," Strachan noted. "Elliot Anderson was also another one they should have gone for. Tielemans has been doing well in the Premier League for nearly 10 years, so they're buying somebody who's at the latter stage of his career. I might be wrong, I hope I'm wrong, and hopefully, he’s got another five or six years in him.

Sources indicate that "And I've got to say, the world of football in England is full of the top teams, especially Chelsea, Spurs, bringing in players who sign for £40m, £50m, you go, who is he? There's just so many players like this now.

Recent findings suggest that "You see some of these players, and you go, what has he done to deserve a £45m fee? Baleba, Santos, you’re picking up people for major fees, who have no reputation.

In a recent development, "Who's been brave here? Is this just a kind of cosy midfield? You could go back to Mason Mount for £40m - who actually signed this off to pay this amount of money for players?

"It’s just beyond belief the money that Man United have wasted. It's phenomenal. And that's from the recruitment not doing their work properly.

Recent findings suggest that "They've got to start saying, what is my plan for the next 10 years at Man United? And how do we go about this? Arsenal were a bit like that five or six years ago. It wasn't anywhere near as bad a situation as Man United, but they stuck to their plan, and it paid off.".

Data from the 2026-27 season does not paint Wharton in the most positive light compared to his Man United peers, given Crystal Palace's atrocious start to the campaign.

Indeed, the England international only leads Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Mainoo on games played, crosses per 90 and accurate crosses per 90, while also winning the fewest duels and registering the lowest percentage of successful passes.

However, Wharton has committed the fewest fouls per 90 minutes of the quintet, and he has been dispossessed on the second-fewest occasions per 90 minutes, only behind Santos.

Thanks to Crystal Palace's perilous position in the Premier League table - Thomas Frank's men sit bottom of the rankings with just seven points from nine games - interested parties could pick up Wharton for a discount if the Eagles are relegated to the Championship.

The 22-year-old is valued at €75m (£62.8m) by Transfermarkt and has three years left on his Palace contract, but Man United may have to fend off competition from Liverpool and Chelsea to land him in 2027.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27.

Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.

Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.

However, with the Cherries set for a Celta Vigo challenge on Thursday night, it is clear that the Dean Court club are thriving, with the visitors to Spain sitting in fifth position in the Premier League standings.

A star of the current positive form, Evanilson has truly announced himself as an elite top-flight striker, netting seven goals and providing two assists in his past eight appearances, scoring in five consecutive league fixtures.

What makes Bournemouth's run even more impressive is that last season's star man Junior Kroupi has barely started a competitive match so far after recovering from a broken leg sustained over the summer.

Starting with a 3-0 Europa League success over Austrian side Sturm Graz on October 15, Bournemouth have recorded nine straight victories in all competitions across the Premier League, EFL Cup and European action.

That winning streak is the longest since the Cherries became a Football League club at the beginning of the 1923-24 season, showcasing how impressively the South Coast team are performing at the moment.

However, there are still more records to be achieved over the coming weeks, with Bournemouth aiming to become only the eighth team to record 10 straight competitive victories whilst playing in the Premier League.

Winning the Premier League during the 2016-17 campaign under Antonio Conte, Chelsea managed 10 wins in a row in all competitions, with that particular streak running from October 2016 until Fresh Year's Eve 2016.

Leeds are the other club to post that exact number of wins in succession, with the Elland Road side completing the feat between August and October during the 1999-00 Premier League term.

The dominant force in English domestic football during the late 2010s and early 2020s, Manchester City are unsurprisingly the club with the most consecutive competitive wins as a Premier League side.

Under the expert stewardship of Pep Guardiola, the title-winning Citizens won 21 straight matches between December 2020 and March 2021, destroying Arsenal's previous record of 13 games in succession.

To match Man City's record, Bournemouth would need to secure victory in Spain on Thursday before winning every single match up to and including the trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on January 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United cut ties with the striker following their last promotion to the Premier League. SUFC decided not to hand him a contract extension at Bramall Lane and he subsequently became a free agent.

Sharp, now 40, had three separate spells as a player at Bramall Lane. He confirmed his retirement in October but has since featured in non-league for AFC Rushden & Diamonds.

Sources indicate that he has opened up about his departure from his boyhood club three-and-a-half years ago on Sky Sports’ Essential EFL Podcast: “I had a chance about three or four years before (to leave), Colorado Rapids were potentially going to take me but it wasn’t the right time. I didn’t leave Sheffield United. Sheffield United didn’t offer me a upcoming contract which was so disappointing for me because I got told by the owners and by the manager three times that I was going to get another year. I got told on the day of the parade that I wasn’t going to get it which absolutely ruined the day for me.

Industry observers note that “I was distraught. I was going to retire at 37, that was me thinking ‘do you know what, I’ve had such a good career and I can’t see myself playing for another team’. I wanted to end at Sheffield United but I was out of contract for the first time in my career and (then) LA Galaxy came calling.”.

Sharp rose up through Sheffield United’s academy as a youngster and was a regular for them at various different youth levels. He went on to play twice for SUFC’s first-team before leaving for Scunthorpe United in 2005.

Industry observers note that the Blades re-signed him two years later and he scored 13 goals in 64 matches before embarking on spells at Doncaster Rovers, Southampton, Nottingham Forest, Reading and Leeds United. Chris Wilder lured him back to his hometown team for a third time when they were in League One in 2015.

In a recent development, sharp helped Sheffield United rise from the third tier to the Premier League and found the net on 116 occasions in 311 outings. However, his former club didn’t offer him fresh terms under Paul Heckingbottom and he subsequently became available.

In a recent development, as he has now alluded to, he considered hanging up his boots before LA Galaxy came calling. His stint in America was brief though and he later returned with Hull City before Doncaster Rovers brought him back.

According to recent reports, sharp will go down as one of Sheffield United’s greatest ever strikers. He is a legend at SUFC and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see him go back there in some capacity down the line.

According to recent reports, the Blades are currently looking to claw themselves out of the EFL and back into the top flight if possible. They drew 1-1 at home against Southampton on Tuesday night with midfielder Sydie Peck scoring a late equaliser.

Sources indicate that wilder‘s side are sat in 9th place in the table after 17 fixtures and they are only one place outside the play-offs. They are one point behind Swansea City in 8th and could rise into the top eight this weekend if results go their way.

Sources indicate that sheffield United face a tricky away trip down to QPR on Saturday. Their upcoming opponents are positioned in 7th.

Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he mentioned.

Industry observers note that the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Sources indicate that hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Last night, AC Milan added another five goals to their tally in Serie A, making it one of their best starts to a season ever.

With Ruben Amorim, Milan are no longer the defence-first team that Massimiliano Allegri made them. Instead, they’re fluid, attacking and dangerous and the statistics show as much. So much so that their stars are shining brighter than they may have ever done before.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are on fire, so much so that they’ve only outscored this season’s start twice in their history. With 28 goals in 12 games, everyone is helping things tick, but Pulisic, again, is standing out.

After a fine international break, the American ‘led the way’ again and added a goal to his tally for the season in fine fashion. He dons the superhero cape in a team that ‘plays, scores and has fun’ and with him, the team keep winning.

In a recent development, every 87 minutes in the league, he’s contributed and for that reason, there’s a sense of inevitability seeing him in the teamsheet. Gazzetta writes that it’s effectively like entering every game with a 1-0 lead already.

He’s now scored in three consecutive games and it’s form that has not been bettered since the start of the 2024/25 season; where he scored four goals in a row. It’s not really a surprise, either.

In Ruben Amorim’s front-foot system, he’s one of the frontmen and that naturally means he’s going to score and create more. A ‘perfect match’ for Amorim, he’s leading in every sense and you’d have to look to the teams of Nereo Rocco and Lajos Czeizler for more goals – both teams scored 29 in their first 12 games of the Serie A season.

Ardon Jashari grabbing a goal also raised the number of scorers this season to eight, which is impressive in itself. It’s a ‘super-attacking’ team where everyone contributes, but Pulisic is again leading.

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 10:55, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:05.

Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.

Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.

More than six months after Luton Town narrowly missed out on a place in the League One playoffs last season, finishing just one point behind sixth-placed Leyton Orient, the Hatters have made a positive start to the 2026-27 campaign as they look to go one step better this time around.

Wilshere's side began the latest season inconsistently and were sitting 16th after seven third-tier matches at the end of September, but have since enjoyed an impressive upturn in form, losing just once in the league across October and November, a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons at Stadium MK.

That run has seen Luton win six of their last eight league matches, while also progressing to the second round of the FA Cup and the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy, putting them firmly back in the playoff picture.

In fact, the Hatters could move into second place heading into the final month of the calendar year if they secure a ninth league victory of the season and other results go their way this weekend, with their recent form having lifted them more than 10 places into fifth and guaranteed them a place in the top six until at least their 17th league match next week, when they face struggling Blackpool.

A key factor behind their turnaround has been an improvement in front of goal, with Luton scoring 17 times in League One since the start of October, an average of more than two per game that has taken their overall tally to 29, a record bettered by just one side in the division.

As for the visitors, Oxford United make the 66-mile journey to Bedfordshire in similarly strong form and will be looking to move into December in the top two by recording a third consecutive victory.

The U's, led by former Wales midfielder Ramsey, have enjoyed a more consistent campaign than their upcoming opponents, having already moved into the top six by their seventh match of the 2026-27 season, when Luton were sitting 16th, and have continued to build on that strong start in recent weeks to climb to third.

Oxford head into their 15th league outing of the season with 29 points following eight wins, five draws and just one defeat, and they could move level on points with leaders Stockport County this weekend while still having two games in hand on Jimmy McNulty's side.

Although Oxford's FA Cup campaign came to an end at the first hurdle with a 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage, their form in the third tier has been exceptional, with no side in the top four divisions of English football losing fewer league matches than the U's.

Only Ramsey and Wilshere's former club Arsenal and League Two side Barnet have matched their tally of just one defeat.

While Luton have built their campaign around a clinical attacking unit, Oxford's promotion push has been underpinned by a strong defensive record, with only three sides in League One having conceded fewer than their 14 goals.

However, shipping three at home to Wycombe Wanderers last weekend, despite coming from three goals behind to secure a remarkable 4-3 victory, represented a rare blemish on an otherwise impressive defensive campaign.

The pair meet for the first time in just under two years on Saturday and will lock horns in a third-tier fixture for the first time since 2019, with Luton having enjoyed a spell in the Premier League since their previous meeting at this level.

Luton Town form (all competitions):.

Oxford United form (all competitions):.

Luton Town will be forced into at least one change following their weekend victory over Burton Albion after Jordan Clark was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute, with the midfielder expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Daniel Gore.

Clark is set to join fellow injury absentees Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris in the treatment room, with the latter yet to feature at all this season.

Former Bristol City forward Nahki Wells marked his 15th league appearance of the campaign with his eighth and ninth goals of the season, scoring a brace against the Brewers last Saturday, and the Bermudian is expected to lead the line once again.

Having been in EFL Trophy action during the week, beating Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1, Ramsey is expected to make wholesale changes for Oxford's return to League One action.

Jamie Cumming started in goal for the midweek cup tie and could retain his place ahead of Simon Eastwood, who conceded three times last weekend, while changes are also expected throughout the defence, midfield and attack.

Gatlin O'Donkor came off the bench to score a dramatic winner five minutes into stoppage time against Wycombe and could therefore be rewarded with a starting place on Saturday, potentially at the expense of Tyler Goodrham.

Luton Town possible starting lineup:.

Shea; Jones, Mengi, Andersen, Johnston; Walsh; Richards, Donley, Gore, Palmer; Wells.

Oxford United possible starting lineup:.

Cumming; Kioso, Long, Brown, Currie; Brannagan, Andrews; Missanga, O'Donkor, Emakhu; Harris.

While Oxford United arrive at Kenilworth Road in high spirits, they face a side who have collected more points than any other team in the division across their last six league games, meaning the U's will know they face a difficult task to win at a ground where they have not tasted victory since 2017.

With that said, Oxford did manage to come away from their last visit to Luton with a point, albeit more than two years ago, and we expect them to repeat that feat, with the two in form sides playing out a 2-2 draw.

IL MANCHESTER UNITED ESERCITA L'OPZIONE PER IL RINNOVO DI BRUNO FERNANDES. IL MILAN RESTA ALLA FINESTRA.

Francisco Conceiçao, ieri mattatore dell'Omonia con gol e assist, può diventare un uomo mercato per la Juventus. Ovviamente più in vista dell’estate piuttosto che adesso nella sessione invernale. Il tutto salvo clamorose offerte che potrebbero arrivare all’improvviso. L’esterno portoghese per le sue caratteristiche piace molto in Premier League dove ha molti estimatori. E quindi ecco che è una situazione da monitorare nei prossimi mesi. Il Liverpool non ha mai nascosto un certo interesse già questa estate. L’obiettivo era trovare un sostituto di Salah e il suo nome era ai primi posti nella lista dei Reds. Poi il discorso non è decollato e Conceiçao è rimasto in bianconero. A dire il vero nell’ultima sessione c’è stato anche un sondaggio del Manchester United, che però poi non è andato oltre. Adesso all’orizzonte però è spuntata un’altra pretendente. Sì perché il Newcastle ha mostrato interesse e magari a giugno il club bianconero potrebbe anche decidere di intavolare una trattativa allargata con Woltemade. Molto dipenderà anche dal rendimento del gigante di Brema. Per gennaio l’obiettivo principale resta la punta centrale. Il profilo più adatto resta Sorloth. I contatti con l’Atietico Madrid proseguono in attesa di novità. Intanto per il futuro la Juventus segue da vicino gli sviluppi della vicenda legata a Bruno Fernandes. Il capitano del Manchester United non ha intenzione di rinnovare il suo contratto in scadenza 30 giugno 2027 con i Red Devils. I bianconeri sono in corsa (come del resto il Milan) e in attesa di capire quali potrebbero essere i margini di movimento per l’anno prossimo.

According to recent reports, in vista della sfida di campionato di domenica alle 15 a Reggio Emilia tra Sassuolo e Napoli, il nome di Sebastiano Esposito incrocia le vicende di campo con le strategie di mercato del club azzurro. L'attaccante è ormai inserito nel giro della Nazionale guidata da Roberto Mancini e punto fermo degli emiliani prima con Aquilani e ora con D'Aversa. Questo nonostante un avvio di stagione complicato e soli due gol segnati contro Juventus e Lazio, in nove presenze. Seba è uno dei primi obiettivi del direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna e del tecnico Massimiliano Allegri per il mercato di gennaio, dopo un primo tentativo fatto in estate. Durante l'ultima sosta, come riporta La Gazzetta dello Sport si è svolto un incontro a Castel Volturno tra Manna e l'agente del giocatore per valutare la fattibilità dell'operazione, che ha già ottenuto il gradimento del presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis; l'operazione resta complessa poiché il Sassuolo, che detiene il cartellino in prestito dal Cagliari con diritto di riscatto a 10 milioni, necessita prima di un sostituto per la corsa salvezza. Come vi abbiamo raccontato, quello di Esposito non è l'unico nome: il Napoli monitora su tutti Gustavo Varela del Monza, in attesa di capire che tipo di concorrenza si formerà.

Industry observers note that non soltanto Patrick Zabi nella lista dei possibili rinforzi per il centrocampo del Napoli. Il direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna avrebbe messo gli occhi anche su André, talento ventenne di proprietà del Corinthians che da pochi giorni ha ottenuto anche la convocazione nella nazionale maggiore brasiliana. Un profilo di prospettiva, in linea con la strategia di mercato della società partenopea, intenzionata a ringiovanire progressivamente il proprio organico. Secondo quanto riportato dal Corriere dello Sport, la ricerca di un nuovo centrocampista è legata soprattutto alla situazione di Frank Anguissa, destinato a lasciare il Napoli in assenza di un accordo per il rinnovo del contratto in scadenza. Oltre all'ivoriano Patrick Zabi, classe 2006 del Paris FC già accostato agli azzurri nei giorni scorsi, Manna starebbe monitorando con particolare attenzione anche il coetaneo brasiliano. Il quotidiano descrive il talento del Corinthians come “un tuttocampista di qualità che ha fiuto del gol e grande dinamismo in mediana”. Caratteristiche che potrebbero tornare particolarmente utili a Massimiliano Allegri, ma a complicare un'eventuale operazione sarebbe la valutazione economica del cartellino. La recente convocazione nella Seleção potrebbe inoltre contribuire a far lievitare il prezzo del centrocampista e ad attirare l'interesse di altre società europee. Per il momento il Napoli continua a monitorare la situazione.

Sources indicate that il Manchester United ha esercitato l'opzione per prolungare di un anno il contratto di Bruno Fernandes. Il capitano dei Red Devils, che si trovava nell'ultimo anno di accordo, sarà ora legato al club fino a giugno 2028. La decisione arriva dopo che il centrocampista portoghese aveva confermato la sospensione dei colloqui per un nuovo contratto, con entrambe le parti intenzionate a concentrarsi sul miglioramento dei risultati in campo. In questo modo lo United evita che Fernandes possa trattare con club stranieri dal prossimo 1° gennaio per trasferirsi a parametro zero nell'estate successiva. Il prolungamento non esclude comunque una possibile partenza nel 2027, ma permetterebbe al Manchester United di incassare una cifra per il cartellino. Il portoghese continua a essere seguito da club europei (fra cui il Milan) e dell'Arabia Saudita, mentre la società ha già individuato alcuni possibili sostituti. Il futuro di Fernandes era diventato incerto dopo l'esclusione decisa dall'allora tecnico Michael Carrick in occasione della sconfitta per 3-0 contro il Bournemouth, successiva alle critiche del centrocampista sulle scelte tattiche della squadra dopo il ko per 4-1 in Champions League contro il Como. Il 32enne è poi tornato in campo prima dell'esonero di Carrick e ha mantenuto la fascia da capitano anche con Mauricio Pochettino. Mercoledì ha segnato una doppietta nel pareggio per 2-2 in trasferta contro lo Sporting CP. Lo riporta The Athletic.

IL REAL MADRID BLINDA BRAHIM DIAZ: L'EX MILAN FIRMA IL RINNOVO DI CONTRATTO. PSG, TORNA DI MODA JULIAN ALVAREZ: ANCHE L'ARSENAL ALLA FINESTRA, MA L'ATLETICO MADRID FA MURO. IL LIVERPOOL FIUTA L'AFFARE MUSIALA? IN ROTTA COL BAYERN MONACO, MA DIPENDE DALLE SUE CONDIZIONI.

Sources indicate that il Real Madrid blinda un altro dei suoi talenti. La Casa Blanca ha definito il rinnovo contrattuale di Brahim Diaz, che prolungherà fino al giugno del 2031 il precedente accordo in scadenza nel 2027, ottenendo anche un aumento dell'ingaggio. La trattativa, avviata già nei mesi scorsi, è stata agevolata dalla piena sintonia tra le parti. Il fantasista marocchino ha respinto diverse proposte ricevute negli ultimi mesi, manifestando sempre la volontà di affermarsi con la maglia dei Blancos. Arrivato nella capitale spagnola nel gennaio del 2019 dal Manchester City per 15 milioni di euro più 5 di bonus, Brahim ha vissuto una tappa fondamentale della propria crescita professionale al Milan. Durante le tre stagioni trascorse in prestito in rossonero ha collezionato 124 presenze, contribuendo alla conquista dello Scudetto del 2022 e al raggiungimento della semifinale di Champions League del 2023. Il Real Madrid, tuttavia, non ha mai acconsentito all'inserimento di un diritto di riscatto. Nonostante un minutaggio piuttosto ridotto in questa stagione, il ventisettenne sta sfruttando al meglio le occasioni concesse da José Mourinho. Nell'ultima sfida di Champions League contro il PSV Eindhoven gli sono bastati quattro minuti dall'ingresso in campo per servire un assist a Kylian Mbappé. Con quattro passaggi vincenti in appena 258 minuti complessivi, Brahim vanta una media di un assist ogni 64,5 minuti. Numeri con cui punta a scalare le gerarchie dello Special One.

Sources indicate that L'emergenza in attacco spinge il Paris Saint-Germain a valutare diverse soluzioni in vista del mercato invernale. Con Désiré Doué e Khvicha Kvaratskhelia che rischiano di aver già concluso la propria stagione, il club campione d'Europa avrebbe riallacciato i contatti per Julian Alvarez. A riferirlo è il portale inglese TeamTalk, secondo cui la dirigenza parigina avrebbe effettuato nuovi sondaggi per il centravanti dell'Atletico Madrid, già seguito durante l'estate, quando anche il Barcellona aveva provato a portarlo in Catalogna. La posizione dei Colchoneros resta tuttavia molto chiara: nessuna intenzione di privarsi dell'argentino a metà stagione. Anche i rappresentanti del calciatore avrebbero escluso una partenza a gennaio. Alla finestra rimane inoltre l'Arsenal, con Mikel Arteta che da tempo apprezza le qualità dell'ex Manchester City. Nelle scorse settimane era circolata anche l'ipotesi di un possibile scambio con Martin Zubimendi, ma al momento non risultano trattative concrete.

Sources indicate that il Liverpool potrebbe tornare alla carica per uno dei maggiori talenti del calcio europeo nella prossima sessione estiva di mercato. Secondo quanto riportato dal portale inglese Football Insider, i Reds continuano a seguire con grande interesse Jamal Musiala, trequartista del Bayern Monaco da tempo apprezzato dalla dirigenza del club inglese. A rendere particolarmente delicata la situazione sono però le condizioni di salute del nazionale tedesco, che in questa stagione ha collezionato una sola presenza da titolare in Bundesliga. Stando alle indiscrezioni provenienti dalla Germania, nel contratto del classe 2003 sarebbe presente una clausola rescissoria esercitabile a partire dalla prossima estate. L'eventuale operazione comporterebbe un investimento economico particolarmente oneroso per il Liverpool, che prima di affondare il colpo vorrebbe ricevere garanzie sulla possibilità del centrocampista offensivo di tornare a giocare con continuità. Secondo la medesima fonte, Musiala sarebbe alle prese con una problematica neurologica che gli provocherebbe episodi di crisi epilettiche, una situazione sulla quale lo staff medico del Bayern Monaco starebbe effettuando approfondimenti. Il club bavarese sarebbe preoccupato anche per le implicazioni economiche legate all'elevato ingaggio del calciatore. Il Liverpool osserva dunque con attenzione gli sviluppi della vicenda, pronto a valutare un tentativo concreto in estate qualora le condizioni del ventitreenne dovessero migliorare.

It has been revealed that birmingham City are being linked with the La Liga forward ahead of the January transfer window. BCFC have the chance to freshen up their squad with some reinforcements this winter as they eye promotion from the Championship under the guidance of head coach Chris Davies.

Romero, 26, is under contract at Sevilla until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down on his deal in Spain. He has made 11 appearances in all competitions this season and has chipped in with three goals and two assists.

In a recent development, in this latest upgrade regarding his situation this winter, Ficherio claim he has emerged on the radar of the Blues as they eye a potentially ambitious swoop for his signature. The report suggests that talks have already begun with his representatives over a possible switch over to England.

Birmingham City are in the play-offs after 17 fixtures along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City and they won 2-0 away at Burnley last time out. They are back in action this weekend at home against Bolton Wanderers.

Birmingham City’s Luis Vazquez is facing an uncertain future. BCFC only signed him four months ago but he has struggled to make an impact and is reportedly wanted by Racing Club.

Marvin Ducksch could also leave in January. Therefore, the Blues will need to bring in some competition for August Priske up top.

According to recent reports, romero was said to be on Sheffield United and Ipswich Town’s shortlist back in July last year. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put at Sevilla.

Birmingham City could see the Spaniard as someone to bolster their attacking department. As well as down the middle, he can also play on the left flank as well if needed.

Romero has enjoyed plenty of game time at Sevilla in the Spanish top flight over recent years and would be an eye-catching addition for Birmingham City if they managed to get him through the entrance door. He would inject more quality into BCFC’s options going forward.

Industry observers note that the Andalusia-born man rocked up at Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan back in 2019. He then broke into the first-team 2023 and has since been a regular.

In a recent development, davies’ men will be full of confidence after their victory at Burnley. They will be eager for more of the same against Bolton Wanderers as they look to close the gap on Middlesbrough, Stoke City and Wolves.

AC Milan treated fans in San Siro and across the world to a dominant display on Sunday night, as they beat Frosinone 5-1.

In recent seasons, a significant win against the visitors may have gone under the radar. However, Milan picked apart a side that was in the European places before the start of this weekend’s action. It’s a huge result.

Of course, the opposition’s playing style helped the Rossoneri a little bit; that can’t be denied. Yet, they hardly rolled over and still threatened to take something from the game before the scoreline became so wide.

As you’d expect, our own ratings were really high, with no one scoring below a 6/10 and Adrien Rabiot was given the Man of the Match award. The consensus from you, the readers who voted after full-time, was also that all of the players were really solid.

Industry observers note that scoring 0.4 higher than he did in our ratings, Rabiot was again seen as the MOTM and it’s understandable why. Then, Luka Modric followed with a 7.8 and Christian Pulisic scored a 7.6 to round up the top three. With his goal, Goncalo Ramos scored a 7.3, which is his highest rating from your scores so far. Perhaps he’d have scored even higher if he’d stayed on.

On the lower end of the scale, Davide Bartesaghi was the only starter given below a 6/10, whilst Omari Hutchinson (5.7) and Pervis Estupinan (5.4) were not viewed as impressive from the bench. Nevertheless, it’s a high average for the team.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 10:58.
  • Nice return to Ligue 1 action a week after Paris Saint-Germain ended their three-match winning streak, with promoted Troyes visiting Allianz Riviera on matchday 12.
  • The Europe-chasing hosts remain one of the division's form teams and will back themselves to overcome a promoted side they have beaten in their last three meetings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 10:58.

Nice return to Ligue 1 action a week after Paris Saint-Germain ended their three-match winning streak, with promoted Troyes visiting Allianz Riviera on matchday 12.

The Europe-chasing hosts remain one of the division's form teams and will back themselves to overcome a promoted side they have beaten in their last three meetings.

Olivier Pantaloni and his players faced a formidable challenge against PSG last weekend, with the defending Ligue 1 champions arriving on a seven-match winning streak.

While PSG extended their sequence of top-flight victories to eight, Nice's three-match winning run ended against the Parisians, hardly a disgrace given their opponents' quality and form.

Les Aiglons remain one of Ligue 1's form teams, with their 12 points from the last available 18 surpassed by only three clubs: PSG (18), Marseille (15) and Brest (13).

Back at home just days after PSG ended their eight-month unbeaten run on their own turf, Pantaloni's men will target maximum points to reclaim a European place, with sixth-placed Brest and fifth-placed Marseille sitting one and two points above Nice respectively.

That ambition appears reasonable given the Eaglets' three consecutive victories in this fixture and four wins in the last five meetings, with the visitors needing a strong performance to beat Nice at Allianz Riviera for the first time since 2017.

Stephane Dumont's men will fancy their chances of a positive result as they enter matchday 12 having collected six points from the last available nine.

Their only defeat during that period was an understandable 1-0 reverse at PSG, a performance that offered ESTAC encouragement in their bid to avoid an immediate return to Ligue 2.

Troyes' recent improvement follows a six-match winless run that included five consecutive defeats, with last season's Ligue 2 champions failing to score in four of those losses.

Collecting six points from their recent fixtures has lifted them out of the relegation zone and into 14th, although Dumont's men sit just one point above Strasbourg in the relegation playoff spot and three clear of second-bottom Angers.

While a disastrous weekend could leave the top-flight returnees in the bottom three, that would require victories for Auxerre, Strasbourg and Angers, with the latter also needing a six-goal swing.

Mohamed Abdelmonem (hamstring) and Elye Wahi are doubtful, although the six-goal forward is expected to feature for the hosts this weekend.

Laurent Abergel and Antoine Mendy remain unavailable due to long-term knee injuries, while Moise Bombito is also sidelined with a leg problem.

Beyond Wahi, Jonathan Clauss (three goals, three assists), Mohamed Amoura (three goals, two assists) and Sofiane Diop (two goals, three assists) all possess match-winning quality for the Eaglets.

Troyes' leading attacking threats are last weekend's two-goal hero Antoine Mille and Renaud Ripart, who remain the visitors' only players to have scored more than once in 2026-27.

Brown has been a regular appearance-maker for the Turkish giants this season and played the full 90 minutes on Wednesday night, when the Turkish Super Lig club beat Shakhtar Donetsk in the Champions League.

With his performances catching the eye in Europe this term, Fenerbahce man Brown is supposedly admired by a number of high-profile clubs, including Nottingham Forest of the Premier League.

The report claims that a number of Premier League clubs are keen on bringing the 24-year-old back to English shores, with the winter transfer window opening at the turn of the calendar year on January 1.

Providing encouragement for those sides eyeing up a swoop for Brown, the left-back supposedly has a release clause totalling £19.2m in his current contract with the Super Lig powerhouses.

It is understood that the stipulation can be triggered either during the upcoming January or summer transfer windows, meaning that potential suitors have options in their hunt for the player.

Since a 2-1 home defeat by Goztepe on October 31, Brown and Fenerbahce have strung together a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1), a streak which includes that historic home success over Liverpool.

Brown spent a large chunk of his academy time within the ranks of East Midlands club Derby County, making 27 appearances for their Under-21s side before commencing his professional career abroad.

The 23-year-old started at Swiss outfit Lausanne in the Swiss Super League following a switch in June 2021, playing 43 matches and scoring five goals across a two-year stint at Stade de la Tuiliere.

Derek McInnes last night hit out at his dozy Rangers side for switching off in the latter stages of a hard-fought 3-2 home win over Aberdeen and warned them they will be made to pay over the course of the season if they carry on being so naive.

Goals from Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin in the first ten minutes of the second half put the Ibrox outfit in total command after Brad Lyons had put the visitors a goal up at the break.

However, Findlay Marshall made it a nervy finish for Rangers after scoring for the Dons on 58 minutes and it took a brilliant save from keeper Ivor Pandur to deny Nicky Devlin before Rangers saw it out to take their unbeaten run to 14 games and close the gap on Celtic at the head of the Premiership to just one point.

Industry observers note that ‘I am relieved to win,’ said manager McInnes, who made three changes and altered the shape at the interval. ‘I thought we only played with the intelligence, speed and intensity for about 20 minutes and, in that period, indicated how good we can be.

It has been revealed that ‘But we put the game at risk. We lost a cheap goal and weren’t aggressive enough. We lost two goals, really, from set-plays.

‘At 3-1 up against a team as game as Aberdeen were — and they were really good value — our naivety for the second goal is beyond me.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes was relieved to win but urges his side to keep focused.

Nicolas Raskin slots home the third goal for Rangers in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen.

‘I am not sure it was a free-kick in the first place, but we turn our backs. It is almost as if we are in a daydream and we allow them to manipulate the ball. Great finish from wee Findlay Marshall, but we put ourselves in the mire there by just knocking off.

‘We were so naive at times in the game. We scored good goals at good times but I still think Aberdeen will be disappointed not to get something.

It has been revealed that ‘We should have stayed in charge of the game and the second goal we lose allows Aberdeen to keep going with a bit of oxygen and carry a threat. I am disappointed with the lack of control in the game and I am not really happy with a lot of what we saw.

‘That has to change because we will not always be able to outscore the opposition.

‘We hit Aberdeen like a train in the second half and they found themselves 3-1 down because of the quality and intelligence of our play. For whatever reason, we then started playing back the way again. We played more passbacks to my goalkeeper than I can remember in a long time.

It has been revealed that ‘We need to play forward and show more control in the game. I am looking for better from my team.’.

Raskin, meanwhile, has urged his Rangers team-mates to blast themselves to the top of the table on Saturday night and really pile the pressure on arch-rivals Celtic.

The Light Blues play host to third-placed Falkirk on Saturday afternoon with Celtic going to Hearts the following day and the Belgian midfielder wants to make sure they don’t let the defending champions off the hook the way they have in previous years.

‘We need to keep it going,’ remarked Raskin. ‘In recent years, we have not been able to put enough pressure on the other team and now we are doing it, so that is good.

‘We will see how everybody reacts after next Saturday.’.

Djeidi Gassama scored to complete a stunning turaround for Rangers early in the second half.

Raskin has also revealed it took a stern half-time team talk from manager McInnes along with those substitutions to spark his side into life after a dreadful first-half performance.

‘I think we made the game hard for ourselves in the first half,’ stated the Belgian. ‘The manager had an honest discussion in the dressing room and we came back and scored two early goals, which helped. But we weren’t focused enough after the third goal and conceded to make it even harder.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We showed character again. The manager said what a manager has to say when you are losing, playing badly, you are 1-0 down and you have to win the game.’.

Aberdeen boss Mario Frick left Ibrox feeling his side had missed a real opportunity.

Sources indicate that ‘I am disappointed with the five or six minutes after half-time. That hurts,’ he said.

‘We saw a good performance, Rangers were beatable tonight.

According to recent reports, ‘We need more time. We have to improve. We have to talk about those ten minutes. After 3-1 down, we came back and we believed in ourselves. We deserved an equaliser.’.

FC Cincinnati play host to Nashville SC on Saturday night looking to book their place in the conference semi-finals of the MLS Cup playoffs.

The home side hold a 1-0 advantage in the best-of-three tie having earned a surprise victory on away soil in the opening fixture.

Having booked their place in the MLS Cup playoffs as far back as September 19, the assumption was that Nashville SC would have too much quality for FC Cincinnati, who finished the regular Eastern Conference campaign with 31 fewer points.

Nashville had also defeated Cincinnati in the final game of the regular season by a 2-0 scoreline on away territory.

Nevertheless, an early own goal from Nashville midfielder Patrick Yazbek gave Cincinnati a 1-0 victory at Geodis Park on November 22.

That marked Nashville's first defeat since September 10, ending a 10-match unbeaten streak that featured seven wins and three draws.

B. J. Callaghan will have concerns that their efforts throughout 2026 are close to going to waste, with Nashville having failed to score in two of their last four matches.

However, Nashville make the trip to the TQL Stadium on a five-game unbeaten run on their travels, while just 11 goals were conceded in 17 regular season away contests.

As far as Cincinnati are concerned, they netted 39 goals from the same amount of home matches, the third best attacking return in home fixtures in the Eastern Conference.

Despite finishing down in ninth place, 10 points came from their closing five fixtures, and Pat Noonan's team have now emerged victorious from five of their last seven games, albeit only losing to Nashville in this exact fixture on November 7.

Prior to the first leg, Cincinnati had the benefit of shaking off a lack of match sharpness through registering a 3-1 win at Orlando City SC in the Eastern Conference wildcard tie.

Meanwhile, Jack Maher could be brought into the Nashville SC backline after Maxwell Woledzi suffered an injury during the second half of the last game.

Yazbek and Bryan Acosta are battling for one place in central midfield, while Warren Madrigal may be recalled on the flank.

Sam Surridge, who has netted 21 league goals this season, has scored five times in his last seven appearances.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • QPR signed Pierce Charles on loan from Manchester City in the summer, following his switch from Sheffield Wednesday to the Premier League giants.
  • As Charles impresses at Loftus Road, change could await in the goalkeeping department back at his parent club.
  • Rulli, 34, is only cover, but Donnarumma has drawn criticism for his shortcomings in possession, given that City need a goalkeeper who is comfortable in helping in build-up phases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QPR signed Pierce Charles on loan from Manchester City in the summer, following his switch from Sheffield Wednesday to the Premier League giants. The 20-year-old was viewed as a big talent before this season, but his starring performances for the Hoops have put the wider footballing world on notice.

As Charles impresses at Loftus Road, change could await in the goalkeeping department back at his parent club. The Athletic tips Manchester City to make changes in between the sticks by moving out both Gianluigi Donnarumma and backup Geronimo Rulli in 2027.

Rulli, 34, is only cover, but Donnarumma has drawn criticism for his shortcomings in possession, given that City need a goalkeeper who is comfortable in helping in build-up phases. This is undoubtedly Charles’ standout attribute, and it may well see him accelerated into first-team contention at the Etihad Stadium.

In a recent development, to make it clear, there is nothing suggested about a Charles recall from QPR in The Athletic’s new report. In October, it was confirmed that Manchester City have an option to bring him back in January if they wish, but there were no prepares at the time.

Regular EFL viewers have known about Charles’ potential for some time. He emerged on the first-team stage at Sheffield Wednesday and quickly impressed with his distribution, showing composure beyond his years and a passing range that wouldn’t look out of place in midfield.

Those same attributes in possession have been on show with the Hoops, but Charles is growing in confidence in commanding his box and claiming crosses too. A save percentage of 67.8% shows there is still room for improvement with regard to shot-stopping (FotMob).

Recent findings suggest that however, Charles’ passing abilities make him an ideal fit for Manchester City’s style, and he seems bound to get a chance in the future. Accuracy is one thing, but the Northern Irishman’s technique sees means he can play flat balls into the attackers too, allowing them to bring it down on their chest or with their feet rather than challenging for headers with massive Championship centre-backs.

This allows QPR to get the ball forward quickly and keep it there. It is a rare ability in goalkeepers, and one that will not go unnoticed at Manchester City.

Industry observers note that manchester City need a goalkeeper comfortable in build-up, and Charles is just that. However, at this moment in time, it would be a big risk to pull him from his QPR loan and throw him into the starting lineup.

As touched on before, his save percentage shows he still needs to improve as a shot-stopper. The progress he is making in West London suggests he can grow and become a starting option for City further down the line, but at present, the areas he still has to improve could be exposed at an elite level.

It means the Hoops should be confident of keeping Charles for the season – it would be best for him to stay for the full campaign too.

However, in the interest of staying prepared, it might be wise for the R’s to eye potential replacements. That way, if Manchester City do make a bold move to recall Charles, they are ready to act swiftly when January comes around.

  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • Industry observers note that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

Industry observers note that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

It has been revealed that united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent major players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

Sources indicate that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

In a recent development, afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical proposal to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s newly introduced head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their newly introduced head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Industry observers note that was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a substantial team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

It has been revealed that the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the concern then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

Industry observers note that united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Industry observers note that even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

In a recent development, I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

According to recent reports, the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but massive moments in games like that have a big impact.

Recent findings suggest that we did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

Sources indicate that we could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We have to go home with this injustice.

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. In a recent development, and on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the major goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

In a recent development, fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

According to recent reports, it’s a massive final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

It has been revealed that there will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. It has been revealed that both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

It has been revealed that sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

Recent findings suggest that to most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

It has been revealed that rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very key in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

According to recent reports, it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

Recent findings suggest that with Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

AC Milan have made their move for Marcus Krösche and it seems like it’ll be a matter of time until it’s official, according to reports in Germany.

Krösche is maybe the most anticipated signing of the season, with reports linking him with a move to Milan since before the summer. Even before then, the Eintracht Frankfurt Head of Football has been linked with a move to Italy, but it’s only really heated up this year.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, gerry Cardinale has hinted at a move being ready to be completed soon, and he’s not the only one who’s seemed confident of a deal being agreed. Now, it appears that it has been.

This afternoon, Sky Sport Germany reporter Florian Plettenberg reported that a deal between the Rossoneri and Krösche was done, with a €5 million deal agreed to release him from his contract with Eintracht Frankfurt.

He’ll officially start on January 1, but it seems that he’s already been getting to work, according to reports.

It has been revealed that german outlet BILD also reported something similar earlier today, via MilanNews, stating that an agreement was reached with Frankfurt for a €4m fee to be paid. Again, the start date of January 1 was suggested, but it was also written that the date could be brought forward.

Industry News: Palmeiras vs Estudiantes - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (799 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48.
  • Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.
  • The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48.

Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.

The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, are chasing a fourth continental title after reaching three of the last six finals.

Industry observers note that after 58 years, Palmeiras have the chance to renew their rivalry with Estudiantes in a final worthy of the occasion. The 1968 final was decided over three matches: the Argentines won the first leg in La Plata before losing at the old Pacaembu.

Sources indicate that in the decider at the same Estadio Centenario, Estudiantes won 2-0, with goals from Ribaudo and Juan Ramon Veron. One of the goals in Estudiantes’ first Libertadores triumph was scored by the father of the club’s current president, Juan Sebastian Veron.

Sources indicate that palmeiras have not been as dominant in 2026 as in previous years. They drew two of their six group-stage matches, but have taken the lead in eight of their last 10 continental fixtures during the knockout rounds.

In the round of 16, the Alviverde gained revenge on Cerro Porteno, completing a quartet of meetings between the sides this campaign.

Abel Ferreira's men then needed penalties to overcome LDU Quito in the quarter-finals and Fluminense in the semi-finals. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel proved crucial on both occasions, making three saves in total.

After losing the national title to Flamengo last Saturday, Palmeiras fielded a reserve side in Tuesday’s visit to Chapecoense and suffered a 3-0 defeat.

It has been revealed that although the result did not change their position in the Brasileiro table, Palmeiras are now winless in four matches across all competitions. They have also conceded in each of their last five outings.

Like Palmeiras, Estudiantes have also faced the same opponent four times in this edition: Flamengo, the reigning continental champions and two-time Brazilian champions.

In Group A, Alexander Medina's men suffered a narrow defeat at the Maracana and drew 1-1 at the Jorge Luis Hirschi. In the semi-finals, the Pincha held the favourites to two goalless draws before goalkeeper Fernando Muslera starred in the shootout, saving penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta, and Bruno Henrique.

That trademark Argentine resilience was also evident against Universidad Catolica in Chile, and especially across the two quarter-final matches against Corinthians.

According to recent reports, estudiantes have conceded an average of just 0.5 goals per match across their last 10 Libertadores games. Since the round of 16, Muslera has been beaten only twice.

Sources indicate that their main concern is at the other end: Estudiantes have scored no more than once in nine of their last 10 matches in the tournament. A closely fought contest in Montevideo could therefore be in prospect.

Palmeiras Copa Libertadores form:.

Palmeiras form (all competitions):.

Estudiantes Copa Libertadores form:.

Estudiantes form (all competitions):.

Industry observers note that palmeiras’ medical staff are racing to get defender Murilo fit after he sustained a left-thigh injury. If he is unavailable, Bruno Fuchs is expected to join captain Gustavo Gomez and Alexander Barboza in the back three, ahead of youngster Luis Benedetti.

Forward Paulinho is also a major doubt after developing inflammation in the muscle and bone tissue in his calf. Even if he recovers, he could miss the Copa do Brasil final.

Uruguay international full-back Joaquin Piquerez was rested against Rubro-Negro but is expected to return on the left in his home country.

Fellow full-back Jefte remains provisionally suspended pending a hearing before the Anti-Doping Sports Justice Tribunal (TJD-AD).

For Estudiantes, former Sao Paulo midfielder Gabriel Neves is still recovering from a fractured arm and is likely to miss out.

Neves joins midfielder Baltasar Rodriguez, who is suspended after being sent off in the second leg of the semi-final.

Joaquin Correa sustained a grade-two muscle injury to his right thigh against Talleres on November 7.

With the usual recovery period around three weeks, the former Botafogo forward is undergoing intensive treatment in a bid to make the bench.

Palmeiras possible starting lineup:.

Miguel; Gomez, Murilo, Barboza; Giay, Freitas, Pereira, Piquerez; Arias, Roque, Lopez.

Estudiantes possible starting lineup:.

Muslera; Mancuso, Nunez, Palacios, Rojo; Piovi, Burgos, Castro, Palacios, Cetre; Carrillo.

With two solid, well-organised defences and goalkeepers in good form, a high-scoring contest seems unlikely.

Palmeiras may dominate possession, but Estudiantes could respond with a set-piece goal if they fall behind.

If the final goes to penalties, Muslera could have the chance to redeem himself after a difficult World Cup.
