💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:46.
  • Aiming to move themselves back into the top half of the Championship, struggling West Ham United welcome promotion-chasing Stoke City to the London Stadium on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Hammers' woeful run of form continued at the Fratton Park base of Portsmouth earlier in the week, whilst the Potters picked up yet another Staffordshire victory, this time at the expense of Millwall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:46.

Aiming to move themselves back into the top half of the Championship, struggling West Ham United welcome promotion-chasing Stoke City to the London Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The Hammers' woeful run of form continued at the Fratton Park base of Portsmouth earlier in the week, whilst the Potters picked up yet another Staffordshire victory, this time at the expense of Millwall.

Back in the Championship for the first time since 2012, West Ham United were expected by many to sit at the top of the rankings and waltz to a Premier League return, however, the East Londoners hit a upcoming low on Tuesday night.

The Hammers extended their winless run to a worrying six matches (D2 L4) at Fratton Park, where a first-half effort from Odin Bailey was enough for Portsmouth victory, with the visitors once again failing to break down a stubborn second-tier defence.

Since the early-November arrival of Scott Parker to the managerial hotseat, West Ham have collected just two points across a quartet of fixtures, dropping down to 13th spot in the Championship table - a staggering 11 points behind first-placed Middlesbrough.

Following three away matches in their past four, the Hammers are back at their London Stadium base on Saturday, when Parker's men will be looking to halt a five-game winless run (D2 L3) at the East London venue.

In fact, West Ham rank 17th in terms of home form so far this season, with the pre-season title favourites last picking up three points in front of their own supporters on September 11, when Wrexham were hit for six without reply.

After placing between 16th and 18th in each of the past four Championship seasons, Stoke City have swapped midtable mediocrity for a Premier League chase in 2026-27, winning 11 of their past 14 league fixtures.

The in-form Potters have now gone seven games (W6 D1) without defeat after Wednesday night's impressive showing against Millwall, with George Hirst grabbing the headlines once again courtesy of a game-winning brace.

After recording five consecutive league victories for the first time since the days of Tony Pulis in February 2008, Stoke have moved up to second spot in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Middlesbrough.

The Staffordshire side managed just six league wins on the road last season but could equal that tally already with success this weekend at the London Stadium, where the Potters last played in April 2018.

That East London clash represents the most recent meeting between West Ham and Stoke, with a 90th-minute leveller from towering striker Andy Carroll forcing a share of the spoils following Peter Crouch's opener.

West Ham United Championship form:.

Looking for his first victory as West Ham boss at the fifth attempt, head coach Parker could make changes from the side that was defeated by Portsmouth.

However, there is little room for manoeuvre at right-back, where Joel Veltman should start in the absence of Kyle Walker-Peters (muscle).

Young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick could play once again, with Danish stopper Mads Hermansen dropped to the bench for the past two games.

Stoke suffered a major injury blow during the win over Birmingham City last weekend, with Djibril Soumare picking up a muscular injury.

In the absence of the influential midfielder, Jack McGlynn could start in a deeper role alongside fellow summer arrival Ethan Galbraith.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Piroe.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, McGlynn, Galbraith, Devenny; Manhoef, Bae, Hirst.

Without a victory under new boss Parker, West Ham's ambitions of an instant Premier League return are fading quickly.

Stoke will be in the mood to take full advantage of a Hammers side devoid of confidence, however, we feel that a share of the points is forthcoming at the London Stadium.

Industry News: John Eustace must consider dropping struggling 26-year-old from Derby County starting XI vs Watford: Opinion

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that derby County are rooted to the bottom of the Championship table coming into this weekend’s games, and there is huge pressure on head coach John Eustace.
  • It feels like a must-win match for Eustace, who has been under growing pressure from supporters.
  • One man who has been near ever-present in the Rams’ struggling backline is Dion Sanderson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that derby County are rooted to the bottom of the Championship table coming into this weekend’s games, and there is huge pressure on head coach John Eustace. However, he remains in post and will lead DCFC for their home game against fellow strugglers Watford on Saturday.

It feels like a must-win match for Eustace, who has been under growing pressure from supporters. The season has been a tough one all-round at Pride Park, but with 35 goals conceded in 17 games, they have the joint-worst defence in the league.

One man who has been near ever-present in the Rams’ struggling backline is Dion Sanderson. Against Watford, Eustace has to consider pulling the 26-year-old from the starting lineup.

Sanderson has made 15 Championship appearances this season, starting all of them. He has played the full 90 minutes on all but two occasions, being taken off at half-time against West Brom and seeing red after 66 minutes in the 1-1 draw against Sheffield United.

Recent findings suggest that sanderson was a hit with Derby County last season and he has proven his ability in the Championship across 169 appearances at the level, so Eustace has good reason to believe the defender can deliver. However, the facts are that he hasn’t this season.

In a recent development, the former Birmingham City man has won only 51.3% of his duels, ranking him in the bottom 17% of Championship defenders. DCFC have conceded 28.13 xG with Sanderson on the pitch (bottom 2%) as well, although this is more of an indication of how bad the backline has been as a unit (FotMob).

Eustace has been limited in his ability to make defensive changes, but that is not the case anymore.

Industry observers note that matt Clarke returned to the team against Wolves, and Eiran Cashin was back on the bench. Those two, alongside free transfer signings Shane Duffy and Jack Robinson, mean that Derby County have the depth to make alterations in a bid to find form.

In a recent development, duffy has impressed since joining, so it could be him and Clarke started in a centre-back pairing. If Eustace goes for a three at the back, it should be the fit-again Cashin or Robinson to join them in the side, not Sanderson.

Derby County desperately need some hope. The 3-1 win over Bolton Wanderers gave them a boost, but consecutive defeats to Southampton and Wolves have dampened spirits again.

As rival clubs make changes in the dugout, DCFC have stuck by Eustace. However, that could change with a home defeat to Watford.

This is a winnable game, and you get the feeling that three points are a must. If not, Eustace could be sacked.

That could prompt changes from the boss, who will do all he can to drive a performance from his struggling side as pressure and relegation fears grow.

RANGERS 3 ABERDEEN 2: Amid all the thrills and spills, McInnes' triple switch sparks second-half revival

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1357 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026.

When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.

Coming just three days after going out of Europe — for the second time — to an ordinary Jablonec team, the slender win Derek McInnes’ side claimed at Pittodrie that day felt like a can being kicked down the road.

In those early weeks, the players looked lost. The manager admitted that he didn’t know what style of football he was watching. The supporters were preparing for a long, hard winter.

It’s remarkable what can come from one scruffy win on the road. From that point to this, McInnes’ men have now gone 14 games unbeaten in all competitions.

In a recent development, they have the League Cup final to look forward to next month. They are now just one point behind Celtic in the Premiership and look eminently capable of putting in a serious challenge for the title. In keeping with so many performances throughout this run, however, this wasn’t particularly convincing. Flat and rudderless for 45 minutes, Rangers were deservedly a goal behind at the interval.

Credit where it’s due, though. Their response at the outset of the second period was outstanding with three goals coming in 11 minutes courtesy of Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

Recent findings suggest that that ought to have been the platform for many more to follow. But the performance slipped back a level. Aberdeen scored once and could easily have scored again.

Raskin (right) and Gassama celebrate after combining to put Rangers 3-1 up.

Naderi capitalises on Muller's mishandling to fire Rangers level at the start of the second half.

In a recent development, it was a truly thrilling match, full of slip-ups, incidents and moments of brilliance. The final stages were a tough watch for the home fans who hoped against hope that they’d see their side ease towards a routine victory.

Recent findings suggest that as at Fir Park on Saturday, though, Rangers found a way and added another win to the ledger. And provided that remains the case in the coming weeks and months, none of the light blue legions will be complaining.

Despite ultimately not having quite enough to take something, Aberdeen manager Mario Frick will have been encouraged by much of what he saw here.

Had it not been for that atrocious spell at the outset of the second period, he’d have fancied his men to take something.

In a recent development, they certainly fashioned plenty of opportunities. It was the defensive side of the game which ultimately cost them.

McInnes drafted in Kevin Kelsy, James Penrice and Ben Godfrey with Dujon Sterling, Tuur Rommens and Kim Minsu dropping out. There was a change of shape too, with a switch to a 3-5-2. For the longest time, it did not work.

Lyons gets his head to Marshall's corner to put Aberdeen in front in the first half.

While Frick kept faith with the diamond-shaped midfield which served him so well in Ayrshire, he made three changes. In came Ayoub Mouloua, Afeez Aremu and Findlay Marshall at the expense of Hicham Mahou, Ante Palaversa and Stuart Armstrong.

According to recent reports, before the game, there was a minute’s silence in memory of the late, great Ralph Brand. What a pity a couple of clowns in the visiting section were unable to keep their mouths shut for that long.

Rangers started brightly with Penrice’s delivery from the left causing chaos. Dan Neil had a stab at it, then Naderi. Aberdeen survived.

Once Frick’s side settled, Nicky Devlin’s cross was met by Marshall. His header was straight at Ivor Pandur.

Rangers’ general play was broken, their build-up more ponderous than patient. Gassama did manage to drop a shoulder and get a strike away but Aremu’s positioning ensured Marius Muller was untroubled.

It has been revealed that naderi was again Rangers’ most effective player, although the bar was set pretty low initially. The Czech’s lay-off invited Godfrey to let fly. His strike was well off target.

It has been revealed that while Gassama got into plenty of promising positions, his crossing continually let him down early on. On the other flank, Badredine Bouanani could not do right for doing wrong.

In a recent development, when the ball broke kindly to Naderi on the edge of the box, Ibrox expected the net to bulge. This time the man of the moment fired over. Rangers’ efforts in the first half were summed up by Naderi being tripped by Gavin Molloy on the edge of the box. Bouanani’s effort from the free-kick was woeful.

It has been revealed that aberdeen were aggressive and organised. And when the moment arose, they went forward in numbers.

McInnes highlights his delight after his half-time changes helped turn the game around.

They edged in front on the half hour after Marshall won a corner which was a consequence of Frick’s men being prepared to back themselves.

Marshall curled the set-piece deep to the far post. Brad Lyons seemed to be invisible to those in light blue as he made a late run. Olwethu Makhanya belatedly reacted but it was too late.

Lyons got enough on his header to beat Pandur and force Raskin to make the block behind his keeper.

It has been revealed that the minute the scoreboard indicated that VAR were checking for a goal, you suspected the Belgian hadn’t done quite enough to keep it out. After a lengthy delay came confirmation of that fact.

It has been revealed that how would Rangers respond up until the break? Not terribly well. Lyons’ crude foul on Gassama gave Bouanani a chance to make amends with a set-piece. This one smashed into the wall. Seconds later, the winger fired well over the top when he ought to have done better.

The Dons could easily have doubled their advantage. Jack Milne carried well and rattled the ball into Kevin Nisbet’s feet. The forward played a smart pass around the corner. Mouloua was only denied by a terrific save from Pandur.

There was still time for Mouloua to be thwarted by the outstretched leg of Makhanya as he moved to turn home a cut back.

Bluntly, it was no surprise that McInnes made three changes at the break. Off came Godfrey, Kelsy and Bouanani. On went Minsu, Rommens and Findlay Curtis. The impact was extraordinary.

Re-energised, within 45 seconds Rangers were level. Minsu’s speculative shot did come through heavy traffic. Still, Muller had to hold it. Credit to Naderi for anticipating the fumble. The instant it bounced towards him, he instinctively lashed it home for his 10th of the season. Subdued to that point, the home fans roared their approval. And they’d quickly be off their seats again.

As Aberdeen’s attack broke down, Naderi played a simple pass into space. Gassama had too much pace for the chasing pack. Did he have the finishing? Absolutely. What a turnaround.

Gassama squeezes his shot under Muller to put the home side ahead just after the restart.

Two goals in 90 seconds then became three in 11 second-half minutes. Gassama did superbly to motor down the left, look up and play in Raskin. The Belgian smashed the ball back across goal and in.

That should have been that. Yet three minutes later, the Dons were back within a goal of McInnes’ men. Afforded too much time on the left, Alexander Briedl picked out Marshall with his cross. Marshall swept it home with his left foot via the inside of the post.

Remarkably, the Dons might well have levelled. Pandur made a fine save when Minsu threatened to turn an Aberdeen corner into his own net. The ball bounced off Nisbet and just wide.

Terrific throughout, Marshall saw a good strike whistle just wide. The fact the Dons made Rangers sweat for the win will be some consolation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Donyell Malen has been a new man since arriving at Roma.
  • Struggling at Aston Villa, Malen joined Roma in January 2026 on a £1.7m (€2m) loan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 12:02.

Donyell Malen has been a new man since arriving at Roma. With the Dutch striker the top league scorer in Europe's substantial five leagues in 2026, can he join one of Europe's best clubs?

Struggling at Aston Villa, Malen joined Roma in January 2026 on a £1.7m (€2m) loan. The Dutch striker has stepped up a level since moving to the Italian capital, and he is enjoying an exceptional 2026 calendar year with 26 league goals.

That makes him the top scorer across Europe's five biggest leagues over that period, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe (21 goals). His current success has not gone unnoticed and led Roma to invest £21.3m (€25m) to sign the best recruit of 2026 permanently.

Sources indicate that malen has not been affected by the permanent transfer and is continuing on excellent foundations at the start of the season. He now has 12 goals in 11 Serie A matches, and must also add five goals and two assists in five Champions League matches.

The versatile forward, who was often used on the flanks at Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, has been installed as the number nine by Gian Piero Gasperini with great success.

The Dutchman's performances are logically starting to attract more prestigious suitors.

With Kane injured at Bayern Munich and Doue and Kvaratskhelia injured at PSG, Malen's name has been cited as a target for both giants.

It has been revealed that the two-time European champions are looking for a versatile forward for January, which is exactly what Malen is. His profile fits Paris's needs.

However, PSG do not want to overpay, and as things stand Roma have no interest in selling their star man, who is under contract until June 2030, in the middle of the season unless an exceptional offer arrives. A transfer in January therefore looks very unlikely, even to Bayern Munich, where he would also make a lot of sense with Kane absent for several months.

On the other hand, if Malen continues in this vein, the approaches should multiply next summer. A move to one of Europe's heavyweights could also appeal to the Roma forward, with the Italian club potentially struggling to keep hold of him and to turn down huge offers.

Latest Update: Bromley vs Burton Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20.
  • Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20.

Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.

After securing promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last May under the stewardship of long-serving manager Andy Woodman, Bromley were expected to face a difficult first season at this level, with the club having every reason to stick by the man who had guided them to two promotions in three seasons and taken them from the National League to League One.

However, Woodman's five-and-a-half-year spell at the club came to an abrupt end in late October after a 4-0 defeat to Leicester City left the Ravens 23rd in the table following 10 matches, a decision that came as a surprise and disappointment to many Bromley supporters.

The London-based side turned to former MK Dons, Charlton Athletic, Oxford United and Salford City boss Karl Robinson, who will take charge of his fifth match as Bromley manager this weekend.

Robinson's arrival was followed by exits from both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy in his opening two matches, but he has since managed to steady the ship in the league, guiding his side to a narrow victory over Reading before they followed that up with a draw at home to Wycombe Wanderers during the week, leaving him unbeaten in League One since taking charge.

Those four points from their last two outings have provided some much-needed momentum ahead of a busy festive period, although Bromley remain in the bottom four with 13 points to their name, meaning a fourth league victory of the season could be enough to lift the Ravens out of the relegation zone ahead of the final month of the calendar year.

As for Burton Albion, they make the journey to Greater London from Staffordshire hoping to bring an end to a three-match losing streak in League One that has seen them slip out of the top half and move dangerously close to the relegation places.

A victory in their final home fixture of October against Leyton Orient was followed by defeats to Wycombe Wanderers, MK Dons and, most recently, Luton Town, with the second of those losses proving particularly damaging as they were beaten 6-2 at Stadium MK.

The Halloween defeat to the Chairboys was at least followed by a 4-0 FA Cup victory over AFC Rushden and Diamonds at the start of November, but that remains Burton's only win in their last five matches across all competitions, a run that has also included a defeat to Notts County in the EFL Trophy.

Although their heavy loss to MK Dons came against an in-form side, Burton's own defensive record has taken a significant hit, with Gary Bowyer's men now having conceded 29 goals in their 16 League One outings, a tally bettered only by their upcoming opponents.

With that said, only two teams in the bottom half of the table have scored more than the Brewers, highlighting that Bowyer's side have an attacking foundation to build on if they can turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

A victory in their first-ever meeting with Bromley could lift Burton as high as 15th and give them a seven-point cushion over the League One relegation zone.

Bromley form (all competitions):.

Burton Albion form (all competitions):.

Having collected four points from his opening two league matches in charge of Bromley, Robinson will be keen to maintain some consistency ahead of the weekend fixture, and he has the option of keeping the same side after coming through Tuesday's draw without any further injury concerns.

Defender Kamarl Grant scored their only goal last time out and could partner makeshift centre-back George Saville once again, unless former West Ham United and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford is ready to make his second appearance of the season after featuring against Reading in what was his first competitive outing in more than four years.

Robinson's relationship with Ravens winger Jodi Jones is reportedly strained following events during their time at previous clubs, and the former Notts County attacker is expected to remain on the bench for this encounter.

As for Burton, they are likely to be forced into a change after Joe Lewis was forced off with an injury late in their defeat to Luton, with the defender expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Jason Sraha.

Lewis is set to join several teammates in the treatment room, with Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers also expected to remain sidelined due to various injury and fitness concerns, leaving the Brewers unable to fill their matchday squad in recent weeks.

Matthew Dennis, however, returned to the team after missing just one fixture and could come back into the starting lineup to lead the line, potentially at the expense of either Mark O'Mahony or Gbemi Arubi.

Emeka Adeile has started just two league matches all season but has scored in consecutive appearances and is expected to retain his place out wide on Saturday afternoon.

Bromley possible starting lineup:.

George; Ifill, Grant, Oxford, Mendy; Pinnock, McKiernan, Conteh, Archer; Whitely, Adeboyejo.

Burton Albion possible starting lineup:.

Addai; Sibbick, Sraha, Tilt; Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adeile; Collar; O'Mahony, Dennis.

With both sides heading into December embroiled in an unwanted battle near the bottom of the table, they will be eager to pick up valuable points, move further clear of danger and build some much-needed momentum.

We expect the pair to play out a 1-1 draw, allowing Robinson to maintain his unbeaten start to life as Bromley manager in League One.

AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1215 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.
  • Sources indicate that the own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

Sources indicate that the own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that in the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

Industry observers note that it was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the upcoming coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

It has been revealed that the vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

Industry observers note that to continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Recent findings suggest that yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

According to recent reports, on top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding latest levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

According to recent reports, needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

In a recent development, it was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Sources indicate that truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

According to recent reports, the American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Industry observers note that then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around swiftly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be stated that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers have maintained solid form since the international break, drawing with Burnley before a midweek win over Watford. They’ve had to deal with adversity ahead of those matches too, notably seeing head coach Tony Mowbray step back from his duties for health reasons.

Injury to Sam Morsy also presented a dilemma for Rovers. Since moving to Ewood Park in the summer, the 35-year-old has emerged as a leader and formed a fine partnership with Kristi Montgomery in the middle of the park.

In a recent development, however, on hand to step up and soften the blow of Morsy’s absence has been Moussa Baradji. After some challenging moments in his debut campaign, the 26-year-old midfielder has delivered when needed and proven his value in the Rovers squad.

Sources indicate that baradji joined Blackburn Rovers on an initial loan last summer, and he had to deal with injury in his first season. His impact was limited as a result, and when he was available, fans weren’t too sold on his performances.

It has been revealed that despite this, the Frenchman was signed permanently in the summer. When injury hit and Baradji missed the first six games of the latest Championship season, many of the Rovers faithful feared a similar campaign would pan out.

However, Baradji has now played in all of the last 10 Championship games – four have come from the start, two when covering for Montgomery during his injury absence, and two while Morsy has been out. The last two appearances have been the best of the lot, battling hard to help Rovers to a point against Burnley before another well-rounded display in the mature midweek win over Watford.

It has been revealed that baradji has brought power in and out of possession in Morsy’s absence. He isn’t afraid to get stuck in and use his stature to muscle opponents off the ball, and his physical attributes, paired with slick footwork, make him a good ball carrier as well.

Sources indicate that the midfielder’s per 90 stats highlight the impression he has made when called upon. As per FotMob‘s dataset, Baradji is averaging 1.30 successful dribbles per 90 (top 9% of Championship midfielders), 9.88 duels won (top 1%), 7.64 defensive contributions (top 8%) and a 75% long-ball accuracy rate (top 4%).

It has been revealed that baradji’s signing came with some reservations, as a deal was initially shelved when his medical raised an injury problem. However, the numbers he posted in a competitive Swiss Super League for a relegated Yverdon Sport side highlighted exactly why Blackburn Rovers were interested.

According to recent reports, and, his recent performances have started to show that he can be a hit in the Championship too. Baradji pairs power and skill to offer a real force in possession, and his work rate and physicality have seen him offer the strong presence needed in the middle in Morsy’s absence.

Morsy will be backed to reclaim his place when fit. But, at 35, he isn’t a long-term option. Baradji has shown he is ready to stake a claim for a long-term spot in the Rovers team.

Despite Cohen and Shaw arguably performing better than anticipated in their surprise role, Lincoln had also only recorded four points from their last 10 games, losing on eight occasions.

A change in direction has, theoretically, been made at the right time, and a permanent successor is expected to be selected ahead of the trip to Cardiff City on December 5.

For now, first-team coach Shaun Pearson and fellow backroom staff members will attempt to guide Lincoln to just their second home win in nine matches, their only such success having come against struggling Burnley by a 4-1 scoreline last month.

As for Wolves, they make the trip to the ProAmpac Stadium having recorded a 3-0 win over Derby County and having had the most shots (39) in a Championship fixture in 11 years.

For all the criticism that has come Cesar Peixoto's way, Wolves remain in third spot with 31 goals and 34 points from their 17 games.

An eight-match unbeaten streak has been put together, the West Midlands outfit picking up six wins and two draws since October 16.

Lincoln may take belief from Wolves only prevailing from four of their eight away games. That said, Peixoto's side have already made trips to the likes of West Ham United, Birmingham City, Sheffield United, Middlesbrough and Wrexham this season, suggesting that it is a far better record than in black and white.

#165654. Tech Report: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5373 w)

Tech Report: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

Industry observers note that “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, noted. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has been revealed that it has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous newly introduced West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Industry observers note that major? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Industry observers note that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

According to recent reports, jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Industry observers note that leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

Industry observers note that A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

Recent findings suggest that [Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

In a recent development, for each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their fresh model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who indicates that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:12.

Peterborough United will be looking to pick up an key victory when they welcome rivals Cambridge United to the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 11th.

Peterborough head into this local derby after ending a four-match winless run last weekend when they beat promotion chasers Plymouth Argyle 2-0.

Harry Ashfield opened the scoring in the first half, before Harry Leonard converted a penalty in stoppage-time to secure all three points.

The win was a welcome boost for Robbie Savage's side, who are fighting for survival and remain in the relegation zone with 13 points from 14 games.

However, they will be looking to carry the momentum of last weekend's win into Saturday's clash, with the Posh targeting back-to-back league victories for the first time since February.

It is also worth noting that Peterborough have a strong recent record against their rivals, having won their last five meetings across all competitions.

Cambridge, meanwhile, are without a win in their last five league games and suffered a disappointing 3-0 home defeat to league leaders Stockport County last Saturday.

Ollie Norwood broke the deadlock early in the second half with a stunning free kick, before Ethan Ennis doubled their lead and Gassan Ahadme scored an unfortunate own goal.

The defeat leaves the U's 11th with 21 points from 15 matches, having suffered just one defeat in their first 10 games before going five without a win.

Head coach Neil Harris has admitted his side have not been "tough to play against" in recent weeks and is keen for them to "get back to being that team".

Peterborough could welcome back Ben Woods and Luca Mendonca on Saturday, but they are both unlikely to start even if they are fit.

Savage is expected to keep faith with the team that beat Plymouth last weekend, with Leonard set to lead the line with support out wide from Bolu Shofowoke and Owura Edwards.

Cambridge may be forced to make at least one change, with the availability of Kelland Watts in doubt after he was forced off against Stockport.

Patrick Bauer could replace Watts in defence, while Louis Appere is set to start up front with support from Zak Bradshaw and Ben Knight.

Peterborough United possible starting lineup:.

Bass; Johnston, Feeney, Hughes, Mills; Jones, Ashfield; Shofowoke, Williams, Edwards; Leonard.

Cambridge United possible starting lineup:.

Eastwood; Perry, Heffernan, Bauer; Bennett, Ball, Mpanzu, Stead; Knight, Bradshaw; Appere.

Peterborough should have renewed confidence after their victory over Plymouth and we are expecting a tight, hard-fought derby clash.

  • Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.
  • Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:46 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:51 EST, 24 November 2026.

Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee, still licking their wounds after an 8-0 savaging at the hands of Hearts on Saturday, revealed plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Manager Marink Reedijk was thrilled to have bounced back from their 4-0 weekend home defeat at the hands of Dundee United, saying: ‘I think it’s a good reaction to what we have done against Dundee United.

‘It’s crucial that you get the three points at home. Again, that’s a major win. I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.

Martin Boyle takes the acclaim after scoring the all-important second goal for Hibernian.

‘That’s not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.

‘The goal of Nicky [Cadden] is one to, we say, put in a frame and put on your wall as a painting. The one of Martin [Boyle] is why Martin is so vital for us. He can disrupt an opponent if they are so organised and so close to each other and so deep.

‘As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs.’.

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend. On a rare start, Togo international Thibault Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan’s lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

Industry observers note that dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them with two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Nicky Cadden unleashes an absolute pearler into the top corner to put Hibs in front.

Cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Steven Pressley’s side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones’ free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

For Pressley, who changed half of his outfield XI following his side’s weekend humiliation, there were also positives to take.

Recent findings suggest that the Dark Blues boss said: ‘We’re disappointed to not come away with anything and to obviously lose the game. But I also thought we restored some degree of pride tonight.

‘Going into half-time 2-0 down, losing two late goals in the half, can be a little bit demoralising, especially for a team that has a bit of fragility on the back of the weekend’s result.

Industry observers note that ‘I thought we responded brilliantly. We showed a lot of courage, a lot of determination, a lot of spirit and, as I’ve noted, I think we certainly restored some level of pride that allows us a foundation to move into the weekend.’.

Millwall vs Burnley - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:18.
  • Both aiming to halt their respective rotten runs of second-tier form, Millwall and Burnley lock horns at The Den in search of much-needed Championship points on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Lions were sentenced to another loss by promotion-chasing Stoke City earlier in the week, whilst the Clarets claimed an unwanted record in their 2-0 home defeat by Birmingham City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:18.

Both aiming to halt their respective rotten runs of second-tier form, Millwall and Burnley lock horns at The Den in search of much-needed Championship points on Saturday afternoon.

The Lions were sentenced to another loss by promotion-chasing Stoke City earlier in the week, whilst the Clarets claimed an unwanted record in their 2-0 home defeat by Birmingham City.

After suffering just four Championship away defeats last season on their way to a third-placed finish, Millwall picked up their sixth loss on the road in 2026-27 at Stoke on Wednesday night.

The Lions extended their losing run to four consecutive matches following a lacklustre first-half display at the bet365 Stadium, where in-form striker George Hirst bagged a game-clinching brace for the hosts.

Winning just one of their past eight second-tier matches (D1 L6), Alex Neil's side have plummeted down to 18th spot in the Championship standings, a mammoth nine points behind the current top-eight pace.

Following four straight losses on the road, Millwall are in desperate need of some home comforts this weekend; however, the Lions have enjoyed victory in just one of their past six (D2 L3) competitive contests at The Den.

One of a multitude of problems facing head coach Neil ahead of a hectic festive period, the South Londoners are struggling in attack since the summer departure of Femi Azeez, scoring only once across their past four matches.

Whilst Millwall are experiencing a saddening fall from grace relative to last season, Saturday's visitors Burnley are in the midst of a full-blown crisis, with the recently-relegated side presently sleepwalking towards League One.

A 2-0 defeat by Birmingham at Turf Moor on Wednesday night made it 24 consecutive home league fixtures without a win for the Clarets - the longest such streak in the history of English football.

Despite this, head coach Fabio Celestini opted for the glass-half-full approach during his post-match media duties, insisting that Burnley bested Blues outside of the two boxes during the Lancashire loss.

The optimistic Swiss boss needs to increase his side's effectiveness in the decisive moments to avoid the same fate as Nicky Hayen, though, as the Clarets are winless in their opening five matches (D3 L2) with the 51-year-old at the helm.

Joining Premier League strugglers Manchester United on just the single league victory so far this season, Burnley are currently occupying 23rd position in the Championship rankings, four points from safety.

After accusing a number of his players of "not taking part in the game" at Stoke on Wednesday, it is safe to say that Millwall boss Neil is planning changes to his XI this weekend.

That indirect jab was likely commenting on the displays of Milhailo Ivanovic, Tairyk Arconte and Jenson Metcalfe, with the trio replaced at half time.

Derek Mazou-Sacko will start in the middle of the park, and influential Belgian Casper de Norre is set to return to the matchday squad.

Zak Sturge's absence reduces the hosts' options at left-back, with the 22-year-old picking up a straight red card during the defeat by Queens Park Rangers last Saturday.

Burnley also have a suspended player for this weekend's clash, with Wales international Connor Roberts out of action following his dismissal at Cardiff City on November 7.

The Clarets could make attacking alterations after firing a blank against Birmingham, with Marcus Edwards and Jamie Vardy pushing for starts.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; Kelly, Mazou-Sacko; Sykes, Neghli, Lisbie; Dykes.

Burnley possible starting lineup:.

Weiss; Walker, Alleyne, Julio, Pires; Cullen, Raghouber; Ramazani, Ramsey, Amdouni; Vardy.

After a soft display at Turf Moor earlier in the week, it is hard to imagine Burnley coping with the physical challenge posed by a trip to The Den.

Millwall were much-improved in the second half at Stoke and should be relatively confident of putting their relegation-threatened visitors to the sword.

Leicester City could lose loan star in January as parent club consider recall

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town.
  • According to recent reports, form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up.
  • Recent findings suggest that howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town. Russell Martin’s side have picked up 23 points from 15 matches, winning six, drawing five and losing four.

According to recent reports, form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up. One of which could be loanee Harry Howell, who Brighton are considering recalling from LCFC, according to Pete O’Rourke.

Recent findings suggest that howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start. In all competitions he has two goal contributions in 13 games for the Foxes.

Brighton are considering a recall to send Howell elsewhere in January in a bid to get more game-time. A host of clubs both in England and across Europe are keen on the 18-year-old.

Sources indicate that howell’s loan spell at LCFC has so far failed to provide the regular senior football Brighton wanted for his development. The 18-year-old England U19 international joined the League One club in August to gain valuable first-team experience after limited opportunities at the Amex.

According to recent reports, martin has acknowledged Howell’s restricted role, explaining that illness disrupted his early progress. The attacking midfielder initially made a positive impression before a virus affected his fitness and forced the club to manage his minutes carefully.

By the time he returned, Leicester had established a rhythm and altered their formation, leaving Howell struggling to find a suitable place in the side.

There have been encouraging signs when given opportunities, including a league goal and promising contributions from the bench in the FA Cup. However, the overall lack of playing time means the loan has fallen short of its primary objective.

According to recent reports, howell was intended to be a key player for Leicester City this season but for a multitude of reasons that has not happened. With that in mind, it is no surprise that Brighton are considering moving him on.

Industry observers note that however, that should not be a real matter for LCFC for the rest of the season. The Foxes have plenty of options in that area, with the likes of Kamari Doyle and Sammy Braybrooke currently in fine form.

Losing loanee Howell may mean that Leicester can go out and bring in another loanee in January with a squad spot opening up. With players like Conor Chaplin, Tommy Watson and Liam Cullen also in the squad, they can likely afford to bring in a play in another area instead of a direct replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot stated after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

According to recent reports, it was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this fresh era.

Industry observers note that the former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

Industry observers note that with five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far.

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn.

— c0mp (@c0mpmilano) November 23, 2026.

Industry observers note that he is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Amorim remarked after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”.

It has been revealed that speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

“At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s notable for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

“I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”.

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”.

The renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the upcoming year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

In a recent development, adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

It has been revealed that now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”.

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:28.

Manchester United have been handed a potential boost in their pursuit of Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo, who is reportedly keen on a move to Old Trafford.

The Uruguay international caught the attention of United officials during Wednesday's 2-2 draw in Lisbon, having been monitored by the club for several months.

However, a potential January deal could prove difficult given the asking price and Mauricio Pochettino's limited transfer budget.

According to Sport Witness, a source close to the situation has indicated that Araujo 'wants to join' United, with mutual appreciation between the player and the Premier League outfit.

United first showed interest in the 26-year-old earlier this year but failed to strengthen at left-back during the summer. Araujo subsequently extended his Sporting contract until 2030, which includes an €80m (£67m) release clause.

However, it's believed a fee closer to £50m could actually be enough to secure his services in the January transfer window, despite his latest contract and substantial salary in Portugal.

United officials reportedly watched him closely during Wednesday's Champions League meeting, with Araujo playing the full 90 minutes.

The left-back has made 15 appearances this season and is viewed as a potential solution to United's problems in the position.

Sources indicate that luke Shaw has missed the last eight matches with a muscle injury, while youngster Harry Amass is also among the club's recognised options. Both players have contracts expiring in 2027, adding further uncertainty to the position.

Araujo's performance against United offered Pochettino an opportunity to assess a potential transfer target at close quarters.

Operating in an advanced left wing-back role, the Uruguayan registered two shots, created one chance, won three fouls and completed six progressive passes. He also made six defensive contributions, including three interceptions, per Sofascore.

It was not necessarily a spectacular individual display, but his all-round contribution attracted praise from the Portuguese press and demonstrated the qualities United could benefit from on the left flank.

Araujo could provide the attacking thrust and defensive work rate required to solve a problem position, although the financial implications are significant.

A reported £50m asking price would represent a sizeable investment, particularly with United believed to have less than that available for multiple positions in January.

Pochettino may be impressed by what he saw in Lisbon, but convincing the hierarchy to spend such a large proportion of their budget on one full-back could be difficult when central defence and striker reinforcements are also needed.

Right, it's time for me to head off.

Arsenal's winning run at the Emirates is over.

Recent findings suggest that they had been on a mental run of wins at home in both the Champions League and Europa League. Like, I mean truly crazy. But now it's come to an end.

Recent findings suggest that they have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat vs Eintracht Frankfurt). Yep, seven years... told you it was mental.

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:37.

Preston North End play host to Norwich City on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that could move them outside of the relegation zone.

At a time when the home side sit in 22nd place in the Championship table, Norwich remain in 11th position despite their prolonged unbeaten streak.

While many questioned why Graham Alexander left a League One promotion bid with Bradford for a relegation scrap at Deepdale, the Preston legend is right now justifying his decision.

Seven points have been accumulated across the last three fixtures against Southampton, West Ham United and Cardiff City.

Preston had been heavy underdogs in all three contests, yet they came through that triple-header having conceded just the one goal.

Although Preston had to battle hard to earn a share of the spoils at West Ham on Saturday, they were ruthless in dispatching Cardiff by a 4-0 scoreline in South Wales three days later.

Despite remaining three points adrift of safety, confidence is growing at Preston ahead of facing one of the form teams in the division.

Such has been the upturn in Norwich's fortunes that they were disappointed to record a 1-1 draw at home to Queens Park Rangers in midweek.

Nevertheless, having won their previous five games, it extended their recent return to 16 points from a possible 18.

Philippe Clement's side remain with three points of sixth-placed Southampton, a position they will take having lost eight of their opening 11 league matches this season.

Norwich have scored 19 goals in eight away fixtures, the joint-best attacking record in the division, while they have won their most recent three contests away from Carrow Road.

Preston North End Championship form:.

Norwich City Championship form:.

Barring any fitness issues, Preston boss Alexander is expected to name the same starting lineup from the Cardiff game.

Preston were 4-0 ahead before substitutions were first made in the 77th minute, and the same players should keep their places.

The likes of Harry Clarke, Lewis Gibson and Liam Gibbs are all expected to remain sidelined.

Meanwhile, Kenny McLean, Anis Ben Slimane, Oscar Schwartau and Jovon Makama are all in contention for opportunities in the Norwich XI.

Jacob Wright, Paris Maghoma and Mathias Kvistgaarden could be the players to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

Preston North End possible starting lineup:.

Nicholls; Hughes, Lindsay, Offiah; Mills, Thompson, Docherty, Small; Devine, Moran; Burgzorg.

Norwich City possible starting lineup:.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Yongwa; Field, McLean; Brooks, Ven Slimane, Musaba; Makama.

Although Preston recorded the most eye-catching Championship result in midweek, it remains to be seen whether they can back that up against a team playing with Norwich's confidence. Therefore, we are backing the Canaries to come out on top, albeit in a match where Preston will continue to show their improvements under Alexander.

Breaking: Birmingham City man’s impressive display offers Chris Davies a new selection headache ahead of Bolton Wanderers tie: Opinion

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co
