💡 Key Takeaways
  • Birmingham City sit 4th in the league after 17 matches and they are not showing signs of slowing down.
  • The most impressive part of Blues’ resurgence this season is their away form, as they have already matched their away win total from last season – and it is only November.
  • This was a huge reason that Chris Davies‘ side fell short of reaching the Championship play-offs last season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City sit 4th in the league after 17 matches and they are not showing signs of slowing down. BCFC won comfortably against a poor Burnley side last night to take their tally for the season to 32 points.

The most impressive part of Blues’ resurgence this season is their away form, as they have already matched their away win total from last season – and it is only November.

This was a huge reason that Chris Davies‘ side fell short of reaching the Championship play-offs last season. A big part of the improvements on the road this term has been the defence. The Blues have conceded the fewest goals in the Championship and kept a sixth clean sheet of the season against Burnley.

On Wednesday, they did so without captain and standout centre-back Christoph Klarer due to suspension. With Dael Fry alongside Phil Neumann, Birmingham City looked just as solid at the back.

Recent findings suggest that there were some questions over how the Blues would handle missing their captain against Burnley after he picked up a suspension against Stoke City. However, Dael Fry was an ideal replacement for Klarer.

Sources indicate that fry has struggled for game time since leaving Middlesbrough. He hadn’t started in the league up until Birmingham City’s match at Turf Moor.

The 29-year-old has had to bide his time due to Klarer and Neumann forming such a strong partnership this season, and despite this, Fry slotted into the backline perfectly. The former Boro mainstay provided the physicality and no-nonsense defending to make him an ideal partner for Neumann’s speed and ball-playing ability.

Recent findings suggest that fry was a force in both boxes as he constantly won headers in attack and defence. He won three of his five duels total and was assured in possession with 41 passes completed, seven of which were into the final third (FotMob). He showed that despite his lack of game time, he is still a top defender at the level.

BCFC were praised for signing Fry on a free in the summer due to his experience, and he looks as though he will still have an notable role to play in the Blues’ promotion push this season.

Birmingham City have had to make a lot of changes this season due to injuries and suspensions. However, they have looked strong no matter who is playing.

There was a clear focus on depth in the summer window. So far, at points, Carlos Vicente, Paik Seung-ho, Max Bird, Ryan Allsop, Ethan Laird and Dael Fry have all had to come in the starting lineup to replace first-choice players this season.

Having top Championship players like coming in as backup options is a huge weapon for the Blues. Fry would be the first choice at centre-back for a lot of sides in this league.

This depth could really help Birmingham City in a promotion push this season, but it gives Davies a tough call on how best to manage Fry, as a player of his quality is sure to be eager to play more football.

Fry is a professional who can contribute away from the pitch, but his quality is clear to see, and it deserves to be on show. Davies will be more than aware of this, and he will simply encourage the player to prove he deserves to find more minutes when the chances arise.

It has been revealed that it is harsh, but Fry likely drops out of the BCFC side for Saturday’s clash with Bolton Wanderers. Davies will have to manage the situation carefully to keep everyone happy and motivated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48.
  • Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.
  • The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48.

Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.

The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.

Xabi Alonso is among several managers who appear to be assessing the versatile VfL Wolfsburg defender ahead of a potential transfer.

The Blues, Tottenham and Fulham are all 'monitoring' Kumbedi, while City Football Group have also been tracking his progress throughout the campaign, according to TEAMtalk.

The right-back moved to Germany from Lyon in August 2025, initially joining Wolfsburg on loan before the Bundesliga club activated their €6m purchase option.

Despite Wolfsburg suffering relegation to Bundesliga 2, Kumbedi opted to remain with the club and help them pursue an immediate return to the German top-flight.

His decision has not prevented his reputation from growing, with Zinedine Zidane handing him his first senior France call-up earlier this month following an injury withdrawal from the squad.

Kumbedi made his international debut against Italy at San Siro on November 12th, becoming the first Bundesliga 2 player to receive a France senior call-up since David Trezeguet in 2007.

Chelsea's interest in Kumbedi could make sense given the uncertainty surrounding their options at right-back.

Reece James' injury problems have created a significant headache for Alonso, with Pedro Neto having been deployed in a wing-back role and centre-back Josh Acheampong also shifted out to the right.

Malo Gusto's uncertain future at Stamford Bridge is another potential consideration, leaving Chelsea with reasons to explore the market for a specialist defender capable of providing greater depth and versatility.

European scouts are reportedly impressed by his pace, athleticism and stamina, while his ability to operate on either flank further adds to his appeal.

That versatility is particularly attractive to a side like Chelsea, who are seeking defensive reinforcements in 2027, with the French gem's performances over the coming months likely to remain under close scrutiny.

However, the west London side are not alone in their interest, with top-flight rivals Spurs, Fulham and City also monitoring the Frenchman.

His international breakthrough could make competition for his signature increasingly fierce, but Chelsea's need for greater stability and depth on the right makes this a potential transfer worth watching.

Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

Industry observers note that "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Recent findings suggest that dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

In a recent development, the two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second highlighted his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

In a recent development, as Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

Recent findings suggest that “A joy to have him,” noted Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Sources indicate that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta states Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

Industry observers note that dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” mentioned Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

According to recent reports, given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

In a recent development, the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

According to recent reports, akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady claims Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

In a recent development, asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta remarked: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some major performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he mentioned. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:.

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little problems that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:.

Sources indicate that “Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”.

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:.

Sources indicate that alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies mentioned Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

Sources indicate that the “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams noted, everything else flows from there.

It has been revealed that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

In a recent development, tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres.

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

Sources indicate that and while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

Sources indicate that when asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”.

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

In a recent development, when asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil stated: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”.

Sources indicate that good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

In a recent development, your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y.

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel.

Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

In a recent development, after the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin concern. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

Team news is expected imminently.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:49.
  • Derby County and Watford square off at Pride Park on Saturday afternoon as two of the worst performing teams in the division.
  • While the Rams sit at the bottom of the Championship table, Watford are only five points ahead of them and with a head coach taking charge of his first Hornets match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:49.

Derby County and Watford square off at Pride Park on Saturday afternoon as two of the worst performing teams in the division.

While the Rams sit at the bottom of the Championship table, Watford are only five points ahead of them and with a head coach taking charge of his first Hornets match.

When Derby travelled to Molineux to face Wolverhampton Wanderers on Tuesday night, they would not have necessarily expected to earn anything from one of the form teams in the division.

However, despite having troubled Wolves during the opening half hour, the Rams succumbed to a 3-0 defeat and allowed their opponents to have the most shots (39) by any team in the Championship in 11 years.

John Eustace has now overseen 11 defeats in 17 league matches, and it is realistic to assume that he may be sacked if Derby lose this game.

In four of their last eight outings, Derby have conceded at least three goals, while they have only netted more than once in a fixture in 13 outings.

On a positive note, the East Midlands outfit did win their last contest at Pride Park, overcoming Bolton Wanderers by a 3-1 scoreline on November 6.

Meanwhile, Watford head into this encounter with former Romania and Legia Warsaw boss Edward Iordanescu in the dugout for his first game in English football.

The Hornets have accumulated seven points from seven matches, hardly a disaster at this stage of the season.

Nevertheless, back-to-back defeats have been posted at Sheffield United and against Blackburn Rovers without scoring a goal.

Despite holding leaders Middlesbrough to a goalless draw before the November international break, Watford have now failed to score in three successive matches.

Furthermore, they have collected just one point from eight away matches this season, that 1-1 draw at Wrexham in August being followed by seven consecutive defeats on their travels.

Derby County Championship form:.

Oscar Fraulo and Bobby Clark are both pushing for a return to the Derby midfield.

Jack Robinson may return to the defence, whether that be as a central defender in a back three or left-back in a back four.

Eustace must decide whether to use Rhian Brewster in an unfamiliar wing-back role for the second game in a row, but Sammie Szmodics remains in a packed treatment room.

Iordanescu will be forced into at least two Watford changes through Mattie Pollock and Jordan Zemura serving suspensions.

Branimir Mlacic and Marc Bola appear likely to deputise, while Edo Kayembe, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma will also be considered for opportunities further up the pitch.

Derby County possible starting lineup:.

Widell-Zetterstrom; Clarke, Sanderson, Robinson; Nyambe, Ozoh, Mowatt, Clark, Brewster; Fuseini, Morris.

Watford possible starting lineup:.

Ravaglia; Traore, Mlacic, Coulibaly, Bola; Kayembe, Kyprianou, Bravo; Vata, Doumbia, Maamma.

Sources indicate that with Watford transitioning to a new head coach, it is difficult to predict how they may perform. Nevertheless, this is a must-win match for Derby and Eustace, and we are backing the Rams to net a late goal to edge this contest.

#165587. Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (936 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious matter.
  • It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026.

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious matter.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

According to recent reports, but this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund.

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors.

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Industry observers note that despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta said: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'.

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an matter which Arteta must urgently address.

Sources indicate that it is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

It has been revealed that he obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

According to recent reports, one back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners.

Kepa Arrizabalaga (right) started in goal for Arsenal with first-choice David Raya out injured.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Arrizabalaga 6; White 6 (Timber 65, 6), Konsa 6, Gabriel 5, Hincapie 6; Lewis-Skelly 5 (Guimaraes 66, 6), Rice 7; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 66, 6); Gyokeres 7.

Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel 6; Gadou 7, Anton 6, Schlotterbeck 6; Ryerson 6, Nmecha 6, Veerman 6, Svensson 6; Bellingham 6, Beier 7 (Guirassy 65, 6); Fabio Silva 6 (Karetsas 65, 6).

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Industry observers note that still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund showed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

Recent findings suggest that after the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more promptly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.

Latest Update: How Ayden Heaven feels about leaving Manchester United as West Ham show interest in January deal

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window.
  • Industry observers note that the 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation.
  • Recent findings suggest that however, his need to play could force the concern and bring a January move to fruition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window. A striker and a left-back is on the WHUFC chief’s radar, and reports have said there is an interest in Manchester United’s Ayden Heaven too.

Industry observers note that the 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation. According to The Athletic, Heaven is keen to play more, but his true desire is to stay at Manchester United, fight for his place in the team and help their battle to rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

Recent findings suggest that however, his need to play could force the concern and bring a January move to fruition. Premier League clubs have made contact to gauge Heaven’s availability and there may be a decision to make over his future in the coming weeks.

Heaven started his academy career in the West Ham setup, leaving in 2019 to join Arsenal. He cemented himself as one to watch while with Arsenal, but a desire to find more first-team opportunities prompted a move to Manchester United in the winter of 2025.

He broke into the side under Ruben Amorim but has primarily played as a backup since. The London-born prospect is held in very high regard, but the need for immediate results at Manchester United means latest boss Mauricio Pochettino would be taking a gamble in entrusting Heaven with a starting berth.

Recent findings suggest that as a left-footed centre-back, Heaven is adept at progressing the ball from deep with a good passing ability and a willingness to carry the ball in dribbles. This aspect of his game was nurtured at Arsenal, and it has helped him slot in at Old Trafford.

He deals with aerial duels well for a player of his inexperience, but his limited senior game time has seen issues regarding anticipation and one-on-one defending arise. Heaven can develop in these scenarios over time though – he just needs regular exposure at first-team level.

A drop to the Championship could benefit Heaven. He would be backed to start regularly at West Ham, likely taking Max Kilman’s place to slot in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos at centre-back.

Playing in a team that wants to challenge for promotion and play possession football would make for good exposure for Heaven. However, it would not be a surprise if his sights are set higher.

Recent findings suggest that heaven is a highly-rated prospect who has already played Premier League football, and he will be confident in his belief that he can deliver at top-flight level if entrusted with a regular role. It could make clubs in higher leagues more attractive than WHUFC, especially on a permanent basis.

The Hammers should keep track on his situation, but be aware that they could be outdone if the door does open for Heaven to move on from Old Trafford.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim became the AC Milan head coach in the summer, but he was far from the only name the management considered.

Calciomercato.com have published a report revealing some of the background on Enzo Maresca, who became Manchester City’s new manager on July 1st after an incredible successful decade under the iconic Pep Guardiola.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

It has been revealed that “In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” noted the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

According to recent reports, “You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This shows how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he noted.

Recent findings suggest that “If we’re where we are, something needs to change. We need to be a little more courageous. Every time we miss a World Cup or a European Championship, people say everything needs to change, and then nothing ever changes.”.

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.

Latest Update: MK Dons vs Notts County - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:57.
  • MK Dons will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Notts County to Stadium MK on Saturday.
  • The hosts currently sit 10th in the League One table, while the visitors are 19th.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:57.

MK Dons will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Notts County to Stadium MK on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit 10th in the League One table, while the visitors are 19th.

MK Dons have found some form in recent weeks after making a poor start to the season and are unbeaten in their last five league games heading into Saturday's fixture.

Paul Warne's side failed to win any of their first eight league matches, but have now won five of their last seven after picking up their first victory over Luton back in October.

The Dons won four successive league games, scoring a whopping 17 goals in the process, before being held to a 1-1 draw by Mansfield Town last Saturday.

Michael Smith put Mansfield ahead in the first half, but Callum Paterson rescued a late draw for MK Dons with a headed goal in the 80th minute.

However, it is worth noting that MK Dons have failed to beat Notts County in their last six meetings across all competitions.

Notts County are looking to get back to winning ways after suffering a narrow 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage last weekend.

The Magpies should have taken the lead after they were awarded a penalty late in the game, but Conor Grant's effort was saved by Tommy Setford before Josh Magennis scored the winner for Stevenage in the 86th minute.

That defeat leaves Martin Paterson's side with 14 points from 13 matches, with the head coach describing the defeat as a "hammer blow" and admitting his side are "not good enough to have a day off".

Paterson will be hoping for a response against MK Dons this weekend, knowing that Notts County could slip into the relegation zone if they lose and results elsewhere go against them.

MK Dons form (all competitions):.

Notts County form (all competitions):.

Paterson is expected to start up front after scoring against Mansfield and he will likely be partnered by Aaron Collins, who is the division's leading scorer with 13 goals from 14 games.

Dan Crowley, Ryan Wintle and Alex Gilbey are set to continue in midfield.

Notts County are expected to stick with Daniel Kanu as their lone striker, having scored twice in his last four league appearances.

Scott Robertson and Dean Campbell are likely to start in midfield, with Callum Roberts and Luka Smyth featuring further forward.

MK Dons possible starting lineup:.

Dennis; Ekpiteta, Goode, Sanders; Silvera, Crowley, Wintle, Gilbey, Campbell; Paterson, Collins.

Notts County possible starting lineup:.

Belshaw; Gibbons, Ness, Bedeau; Samuels-Smith, Robertson, Campbell, Evans; Roberts, Smyth; Kanu.

MK Dons are one of League One's form sides and they have been incredibly prolific in front of goal, which means they should have enough to beat Notts County.

Looking to gain ground in the race for automatic promotion, West Bromwich Albion welcome Bristol City to The Hawthorns for a Championship contest on Saturday afternoon.

The Baggies are in the midst of an impressive unbeaten run in the second tier, making them the favourites with the best UK betting apps 2026 to record victory over the out-of-form Robins.

Since a 1-0 defeat by Birmingham City at The Hawthorns on October 10, West Brom have strung together an eight-game unbeaten streak (W5 D3) in the Championship, beating Bolton Wanderers last time out.

Wednesday night's match at the Toughsheet Community Stadium provided the stage for Albion's Norwegian stars to shine, with Aune Heggebo (2) and Felix Horn Myhre scoring in a 3-1 success over the Wanderers.

Now boasting the best away record in the division with 17 points collected from nine outings, James Morrison's side are back at The Hawthorns this weekend, when they will be striving for a repeat of their 3-0 battering of Millwall in the Black Country prior to the international break.

One of four Midlands clubs inside the top five of the Championship standings after 17 matches, West Brom are occupying fifth spot in the table, just three points behind pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke City.

Scoring an eye-catching eight goals across their past three league fixtures, the Baggies pose danger from an array of positions, with five different players scoring three or more Championship goals so far this term.

Following three consecutive losses at the beginning of their tricky November schedule, Bristol City stopped the rot with a respectable 1-1 draw with Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night.

It looked as if the Robins were hurtling towards their ninth defeat of the league campaign when Joe Worrall opened the scoring early on, but Cameron Pring's first goal in nearly three years secured a share of the spoils.

Winning just one of his past nine second-tier contests (D3 L5) in charge, Michael Skubala remains under severe pressure at Bristol City, who currently reside in an uninspiring 16th place in the table.

The Robins' sole victory in their current wretched run arrived on the road at Bolton on October 31, when Dom Ballard, Sam Bell and playmaker Scott Twine netted in a five-goal thriller.

Firing an attacking blank in five of their past eight matches ahead of Saturday's trip to The Hawthorns, there is no doubting that the Robins are failing to maximise the potential of Ballard and Lorent Tolaj, with the pair scoring 40 goals combined in League One last term.

Bristol City Championship form:.

The attacker joins midfielder Ousmane Diakite (calf) in the Albion treatment room, with the Mali international expected to be out until late December.

Right-back Noah Galves (knee) will not play again this season, whilst talented youngster Rabby Nzingoula is suspended for this weekend after collecting his fifth yellow card of the term at Bolton.

There was a serious injury scare for Bristol City on Tuesday night, when centre-back Luke McNally was forced off due to a knee problem.

The 27-year-old has previously missed nearly two years due to a problem with the same knee, meaning that Rob Dickie is likely to be drafted into the XI at The Hawthorns.

Sam Greenwood and Lisav Eissat were surprise omissions from the matchday squad last time out but could return to the fold on Saturday.

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Campbell, Styles; Tunde, Horn Myhre, Molumby, Whitwell; Morgan, Heggebo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:58 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.

The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.

He was yet to score in Europe this campaign for a Napoli side who had been struggling to even reach the play-off qualification spots, but that all changed on Tuesday night.

Hojlund opened the scoring after half-time of the 2-2 draw when he fired low past Gianluigi Donnarumma to condemn City to a 10th game in a row conceding a goal.

He had been found in exquisite fashion by former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour, before turning Marc Guehi and finishing well.

And his celebration caught the eye, as he held up one finger and appeared to shout 'one team in Manchester' in the direction of the home fans.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund taunted Manchester City fans after scoring against them on Tuesday.

Hojlund did well to take on a pass from Billy Gilmour before firing low into the goal.

After the game, he confirmed he did indeed jibe at Enzo Maresca's side but insisted it was all in good faith.

'Yeah, it's good banter,' he noted on TNT Sports. 'There's a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

Sources indicate that 'That's my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.'.

The strike was Hojlund's third goal of the season in 11 games as he continues to try and find his feet again after a disastrous spell in England.

Having arrived from Atalanta as a 20-year-old three years ago, there were hopes he would be the man to lead the Red Devils' forward line for years to come.

In his first season, he scored 17 goals in all competitions, including 10 in the Premier League, but things went downhill rapidly.

He would only score another nine goals for the club before being shipped out on loan to Napoli halfway through last season. In total, he netted 26 times for United in 95 games.

In the summer, he joined Napoli permanently, with the Italians coughing up £38m - a £34m loss for United, who are 19th in the Premier League.

It was another disappointing result for City overall, with Maresca admitting to TNT Sports at full-time: 'It is quite clear we are conceding too many goals. It is something we need to adjust, and we are able to adjust that.'.

  • Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.
  • The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09.

Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.

The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.

Le Havre's 14th-placed finish last season, just three points above Nice in the relegation playoff spot, offered little encouragement ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and those concerns have proved justified.

Le Club Doyen have not won a top-flight fixture since beating Lorient 2-0 on the final day of last season, with their miserable start prompting Didier Digard's dismissal at the end of October.

Valerien Ismael's first match in charge of the basement club began brightly when Josh Maja scored after three minutes against Troyes; however, they held that advantage for just 15 minutes before eventually losing 3-1.

Conceding three more goals left Les Ciel et Marine with the competition's joint-worst defensive record, having shipped 25, while their tally of 10 scored surpasses only Angers' nine.

Even victory would do little to transform the Dean Club's position, as they enter this weekend eight points behind the relegation playoff spot and nine adrift of safety.

Nonetheless, the hosts must avoid defeat to Vitor Matos's Strasbourg, who occupy that playoff position.

Le Racing's disappointing start has already cost Hugo Oliveira his job, with Matos replacing his Portuguese compatriot during the international break.

The new manager's debut did not go to plan, with Le RCS losing 1-0 to Brest despite an encouraging performance in which they attempted 15 shots to their opponents' 16; Le Racing also created two chances deemed clear-cut to Brest's one.

Looking to build on that display, Le RCS target their fourth victory of the campaign this weekend, although it would be only their second since early October.

Maximum points could lift Matos's men out of the playoff spot and as high as 13th, although escaping the bottom three also requires Auxerre, Troyes or Le Mans to slip up.

The hosts have several absentees, with Felix Mambimbi (Achilles), Timothee Pembele (muscle), Rassoul Ndiaye (muscle), Daren Mosengo (ankle), Stephan Zagadou (ACL), Sota Nakamura (leg) and Lionel Mpasi (Achilles) all sidelined.

Enzo Koffi begins a two-match suspension following his late dismissal against Troyes last weekend, ruling him out of Saturday's encounter and December's trip to Lens.

Only six players have surpassed Maja's five league goals this season, but the Nigerian's efforts have brought little reward for a Dean Club side repeatedly undermined by defensive frailties.

Strasbourg have several potential game-changers, with Gessime Yassine registering four goals and three assists, Giovanni Reyna scoring three, Conrad Harder and Dario Essugo contributing two goals and an assist and Sebastian Nanasi setting up three.

However, Reyna is unavailable due to a muscle problem, while Fabio Balde (leg), Oso (knock) and Joaquin Panichelli (ACL) are also sidelined.

Le Havre possible starting lineup:.

Bodart; Sasso, Seko, Touba; Ouziad, Mwanga, Ebonog, Richardson, Jelert; Maja, Fofana.

Strasbourg possible starting lineup:.

Jorgensen; Antwi, Doukoure, Coulibaly, Hogsberg; Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Nanasi, Godo; Harder.

Maja's scoring form offers Le Havre some encouragement, but conceding 25 goals in 11 matches suggests that their defensive problems remain too pronounced for an immediate recovery.

Strasbourg created enough chances to trouble Brest in Matos's first match and should find greater reward against the division's joint-leakiest defence.

#165555. Tech Report: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

Tech Report: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.
  • Recent findings suggest that for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation.
  • In a recent development, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation. Basic research is undertaken mostly by universities and academia, and private industry leads the translation of research into health solutions1.

In a recent development, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success. In 2022, the pharmaceutical sector contributed US$2.3 trillion — or around 1.7% — to global gross domestic product (GDP) and supported 75 million jobs2.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

It has been revealed that however, market failures have been common. Companies have underinvested in developing therapeutics for common diseases with poorly understood biological mechanisms, such as depression, anxiety and kidney disease, because they consider them too commercially risky or unprofitable to pursue3.

Sources indicate that to address this gap, we propose an adapted innovation model based on mission-driven public–private partnerships (PPPs), in which government acts as a leading strategic investor. By bringing together the best scientists in academia and industry and lowering risks in industry development in areas of public need and for diseases with limited understanding, this model would accelerate translation, advance health and increase economic returns.

Industry observers note that here, we outline how it would work. It will require systems to ensure affordable access to drugs and therapies, as well as revenue sharing between public and private partners to guarantee public benefits and to support investments in innovation.

Sources indicate that complex diseases that affect swathes of the population create persistent health and economic burdens. Yet, the current biomedical innovation model has proved limited in addressing evolving health needs. Because private investment is guided by assessments of risk and return, it tends to favour diseases with well-defined biological mechanisms and high commercial potential. Diseases that are biologically complex, varied or associated with uncertain markets remain underexplored.

For example, in 2023, more than 300 million people globally had depression. The condition will cost the global economy an estimated $12 trillion between 2025 and 20504. In the United States in 2024, one in five people reported that they had received a diagnosis of major depressive disorder during their lifetime, resulting in an economic burden of $334 billion annually across health-care, household-related and workforce costs5. Yet, the leading drug class for depression (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) has remained unchanged since the 1970s6.

The grand strategy to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

The grand proposal to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

Industry observers note that other chronic diseases impose similarly large burdens. For example, chronic kidney disease affects around 800 million people worldwide — nearly one in seven — and is projected to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2040 if current trends continue7,8. Yet, existing therapies cannot stem its toll on human lives.

According to recent reports, antimicrobial resistance is another example, which is associated with 4.7 million deaths globally each year and could contribute to 10 million deaths annually by 2050. Increased treatment costs for people with resistant infections amount to $1 trillion every year9. The antibiotic development pipeline has been depleted over time as economic factors render companies’ return on investment lower than that for other drug classes9. These factors include insufficient funding for research and challenging business models, given the short duration of antibiotic treatments and the need to reserve successful newly introduced antibiotics as drugs of last resort, to be used after all other options have failed.

Industry observers note that bringing a therapy to market from discovery can take 10–15 years and cost anywhere between $880 million and $2.3 billion10,11. The majority (90%) of drug candidates fail after entering clinical studies, clinical trials and drug-approval processes12. And companies won’t invest if they are unsure whether a drug will be profitable.

It has been revealed that consequently, many diseases and conditions have no or few available therapies or only modestly effective options13. What’s needed is a mission-driven strategy to guide scientific capabilities and industry development towards areas of public need by elucidating biological mechanisms and aligning incentives for diseases in which market forces alone are insufficient14.

We propose addressing this misalignment of incentives by reconceptualizing the government’s role in therapeutic advancement through a model of mission-driven PPP. Complementing existing grant-based systems, the model would position the government as a principal investor in select areas of therapeutic development.

The government would thus influence which areas of health and science receive concentrated attention and how successful outcomes are deployed for the public good. Such a model could address specific national needs and global challenges. Here are seven components.

Technicians at work in a pharmaceutical factory.Credit: Getty.

Select disease targets. We propose the establishment of a government-appointed independent advisory body or commission tasked with identifying priority disease targets using transparent, evidence-based criteria, including disease burden, economic cost, scientific readiness and demonstrable market failure. Further criteria to gauge and consider public input into the selection process could be implemented to ensure public trust.

Set up collaborations. A national government, acting alone or as part of an international consortium, would assume a leading role in supporting basic research into biological mechanisms. It would do so by bringing together basic scientists from academia and translational experts from industry to reduce risks in translational development. Private industry would contribute expertise in drug development, clinical trials, regulatory strategy, manufacturing and commercialization.

Provide initial investments. The proposed PPP would not replace existing grant-based systems or market-driven innovation; rather, it would act as a complement by targeting disease areas in which market risks and incentives consistently fail to generate sufficient private investment. The approach could yield fresh therapies and reduce the cost of care to society while generating revenue from upcoming products.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Industry observers note that in the United States, we propose a federal investment of one billion dollars annually over ten years, directed to specific disease areas. That is less than 1.8% of total US government spending on biomedical research, which was $54.5 billion in 2024. This would be supplemented by smaller investments of 10–20% of one billion dollars from a consortium of philanthropic foundations and industry partners joining the initiative in response to a request for application. Given the high costs of bringing a new drug to market, a $10-billion total investment should provide the scale and time needed to pursue about three major disease targets10–12.

In a recent development, feed revenues back in. Public return is a defining feature of the PPP. Existing biomedical funding structures are mainly grant making, with the implication that public benefit will emerge indirectly through the downstream health improvements and economic growth spurred by discovery. By contrast, this PPP framework would directly incorporate public accountability as well as returns.

The government would need to leverage its status as a majority investor to ensure access, fair pricing and affordability. It might require conditions such as agreements to ensure access. Pricing frameworks could incorporate a value-based approach to pricing, in which health insurers offer reimbursements determined by a drug’s value for patients. Affordability conditions, such as reasonable-pricing clauses, would also serve as powerful leverage.
